page: Add and manage tabs in channels and direct messages

section.title: Create a tab
content: Create tabs to feature content prominently in a channel or DM. You can create up to 15 tabs for the following types of content:
Canvases and lists Workflows Messages Links and other files (in folders)

section.title: Add a canvas or a list
content: From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the plus sign at the top of the conversation, then select Canvas or List from the menu. Search for and select a canvas or list, or create a new one if you’d like. If you’re adding a list, select a view . Click Insert . Review the access permissions , then click Share .
Tip: Highlight a canvas or list in a channel or DM by dragging and dropping it into the conversation header.

section.title: Add a workflow
content: From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the plus sign at the top of the conversation, then select Workflows from the menu. Search for and select a workflow, or create a new one if you’d like. Click Add . Review the access permissions, then click Save .

section.title: Pin a message
content: When you pin an important message to a channel or a DM, it will be added to the Pins tab. Here’s how:
Free plan
Pro, Business+, and Enterprise plans

From your desktop, hover over the message you’d like to add. Click the three dots icon . Select Pin to channel or Pin to this conversation in a DM. To remove a message, open the Pins tab and hover over the message. Click the three dots icon , then select Un-pin from channel .

From your desktop, hover over the message you’d like to add. Click the three dots icon . Hover over Organize , then select Pin to channel or Pin to this conversation in a DM. To remove a message, open the Pins tab and hover over the message. Click the three dots icon , then select Un-pin from channel .

section.title: Add a folder
content: If people use your channel to find a particular set of resources (like onboarding materials or project plans), create a folder to organize all of the relevant links and files. You can add up to 100 items or folders per channel.

From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the plus sign at the top of the conversation, then select Folder . Enter a name for your folder and click Create . Click Add , then select an option from the menu.

section.title: Add a file
content: From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click an existing folder or create a new one. Click the plus sign at the top of the folder, then select File . Select a file, then click Add File . Click Share to grant access to everyone in conversation.

section.title: Add a link
content: From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the plus sign at the top of the conversation, then select Link. Add a URL. If you want, edit the display name and emoji. Choose a folder for the link or create a new one. Click Add .
Tip: Add files and links directly to a folder by dragging and dropping them from a conversation.

section.title: Edit or delete a folder
content: Anyone in a conversation can add and remove content from a folder, or rename or delete a folder, even if editing tabs is restricted to Channel Managers .

From your desktop, open a channel or DM and select a folder to open it. Click the three dots icon next to the link or file you’d like to remove, then click Delete link or Remove file . To rename or delete a folder, click the three dots icon in the top right and select Rename folder or Delete folder .
Note: Folders for Channel Expert data sources can be edited, but you can't delete them unless you remove the Channel Expert agent.

section.title: Arrange tabs
content: You can drag and drop tabs in the conversation header to reorder them. This includes moving files, links, and pinned messages in and out of folders. To hide or show a tab in a conversation, follow the steps below:

From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the plus sign at the top of the conversation, then select Edit tabs . Hover over a tab, then click the eye icon to display or hide it, or click the trash can icon to delete it.

section.title: Manage who can edit tabs
content: Channel Managers can allow everyone to edit the tabs in a channel, or restrict editing to only Channel Managers.
From your desktop, open a channel that you manage. Click the channel name and select Settings . Below Choose who can add, remove, and reorder tabs , select an option from the drop-down menu.

All members and guests (by default) Available on all plans

section.title: Share a sidebar section
content: From your desktop, hover over a custom section name and click the three dots icon . Click Share section . Choose the people you’d like to share the section with and review the included channels. If you’d like, add a message to provide context to the people you’re sharing with. Click Share to finish. The people you selected will get a direct message with an option to add and customize the section you've shared.

section.title: Share sidebar sections with user groups
content: If you have permission to create and edit user groups , you can share sidebar sections with a new or existing user group . Keep in mind that you can add one custom sidebar section per user group, and members won’t be able to change the default icon to a different emoji.

section.title: For a new user group
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From the Home tab, click Directories . Select User Groups , then click Create user group in the top-right corner. Choose a name and handle for your user group. Select channels group members will automatically be added to. Under Add group channels as a section in Home , click the toggle, then click Next. Below Add members , search for and select the members you’d like to add. When you’re done, click Create Group .

From the Home tab, click Directories . Select User Groups , then click Create user group in the top-right corner. Select a workspace for the user group, then choose a name and handle . Select channels group members will automatically be added to. Under Add group channels as a section in Home , click the toggle, then click Next. Below Add members , search for and select the members you’d like to add. When you’re done, click Create Group .
Note: You can use the enable_section boolean argument with the usergroups.update or usergroups.create API methods. It's not possible to assign sidebar sections to IDP groups with the SCIM API.

section.title: For an existing user group
content: From the Home tab, click Directories . Select User Groups , then click on the user group you'd like to manage. Click the three dots icon at the top. Select Edit group details from the menu. Add or review the default channels, then click the toggle under Add group channels as a section in Home . Click Save .
Note: If anyone in a user group organized a default channel into their own custom section before the shared custom section was created, the channel won't be moved to the new shared custom section.

section.title: When we'll send a message
content: We’ll send a message to the conversation when the edits to a canvas added to a tab in a channel or DM include the following:
A new heading or new paragraph is added. An item is added to a numbered or bulleted list. A checklist item is marked complete.
Note: Once you’ve stopped making edits to the canvas, we’ll wait five minutes before sending a message to the conversation.

section.title: When we won't send a message
content: To reduce clutter, we'll combine the following edits into the most recently sent message instead of sending a new one:

Additional edits made within four hours of your last edit. An edit made by someone else within four hours of your last edit. Edits made when no other messages have been sent in the conversation since the canvas was last edited.

section.title: Mute canvas update messages
content: If you'd like to prevent edits from sending a message to the conversation, you can mute the update messages.
From your desktop, right-click a canvas tab in the conversation header. Select Don't post canvas updates to channel , then click Save .

section.title: Resume canvas update messages
content: When you un-mute update messages, you'll turn canvas update messages back on for everyone in the conversation.
From your desktop, right-click a canvas tab in the conversation header. Select Post canvas updates to channel .
Note: On channels that have posting permissions enabled, updates to the canvases in tabs won't be sent to the channel.
All members and guests with permission to post in the conversation All plans

page: Guide to AI features in Slack

section.title: What to expect
content: The AI features available to you depend on your Slack plan, your role (member or guest ), and whether your admins have restricted access . AI-generated responses will only include information available to you (ex., messages and other content from public channels, private channels you belong to, and your direct messages). Slack is committed to data security and privacy, and upholding these commitments is fundamental to everything we do. Visit Security for AI features in Slack for an overview.

section.title: Feature availability by plan
content: Note: If you're on the legacy version of Business+ or the Enterprise Grid plan without the Slack AI add-on, you'll only have access to the Pro features listed above. For more details, visit Updates to feature availability and pricing for Slack plans .

section.title: Summarize conversations
content: Get up to speed more quickly in any channel , direct message (DM) , or thread . Whether you’re joining a new channel, returning from time off, or catching up on a fast-moving discussion, AI can summarize conversations in seconds.

images.alt: Generating a summary with Slack AI

section.title: Summarize a channel or DM
content: You can summarize just your unread messages, the last seven days, or a custom date range (desktop only).
Desktop
Mobile

Open the channel or DM you'd like to summarize. Click the three dots icon at the top of the conversation and select Summarize channel or Summarize conversation . Choose an option to generate your summary, which will appear when it's ready. If you'd like, click the More details icon to view the summary's sources.

Open the channel or DM you'd like to summarize. Tap Summarize in the top right. Choose an option to generate your summary. When it's ready, you’ll see a badge on the Summarize icon. Tap it to view your summary.

section.title: Summarize a thread
content: Desktop
Mobile

Open the thread you'd like to summarize. Click the Summarize button at the top of the thread. Your summary will appear when it's ready. If you'd like, click the More details icon to view the summary's sources.
Open the thread you'd like to summarize. Tap Summarize in the top right. When your summary is ready, you’ll see a badge on the Summarize icon. Tap it to view your summary.

Note: Summaries can take longer to generate for larger time frames or message histories. We’ll notify you when your summary is ready, so feel free to take a break or move on to other work in the meantime.
Tip: On mobile, pinch a channel or thread in the Catch Up view to generate a summary.

section.title: Search for answers
content: Ask a question in your own words and get a concise answer based on relevant knowledge already in Slack. Try asking questions that start with “how” or “what,” or use keywords like a project name to get started.
Desktop
Mobile

Click the search bar at the top of Slack. Type your question and press Enter . AI answers will appear at the top of your search results. Answers include citations that refer to the source messages or files that informed them. Hover over a citation to preview the source, or click on it to view the message or file. To share a helpful answer with others, click Share . Review the answer, then click Share anyway to send it to a channel or DM.

Tap the search bar at the top of Slack. Type your question and tap Search or the magnifying glass icon on your device's keyboard AI answers will appear at the top of your search results. Answers include citations that refer to the source messages or files that informed them, and you can tap a citation to view the sources.

Tip: If you're on the Enterprise+ plan, an Org Owner or Admin can enable enterprise search to include content and information from other sources (like Google Drive, GitHub, and more) in search results.

images.alt: Searching for the answer to a question with Slack AI

section.title: Recap what you missed
content: Get caught up after some time away from Slack with a customized summary of your unread channels. With recaps, you can get automated daily summaries for channels that you’re interested in keeping tabs on but don’t want to interrupt you throughout your workday.

When you set up your recap for the first time, Slack will recommend a few channels that you visit often, but don’t tend to participate in, that you might want to include. Once you review which channels to include and turn recaps on, you can mute those channels to keep your sidebar tidy, or unmute the conversations you'd like to continue keeping a closer eye on. You’ll get a new recap every morning with what you missed from the previous day. If you’re away for a longer period of time, your recap will cover however many days you were gone. If you open your recap more than once a day, you can refresh to see any new updates.

images.alt: Adding channels to a Slack AI recap

section.title: Read your recap
content: Desktop
Mobile
Click Recap in the sidebar. Review your recap. Click More details to review a recap’s sources, or click the three dots icon next to any channel to remove it from future recaps.

From the Home tab, tap Recap . Review your recap. Tap a message to view more details, including the recap's sources. To remove a channel from future recaps, tap the arrow icon next to the channel name and select Remove from Recap .

section.title: Manage your recap
content: You can add or remove conversations in your recap anytime, and decide which channels should be muted.

From your desktop, click Recap in the sidebar. Click Manage Recap in the top right. To add conversations to your recap, search for and select the channel you’d like to add. To remove conversations, uncheck the boxes next to the channels you no longer want to include. Mute or unmute channels by clicking the toggle. Click Save .

section.title: Summarize files
content: When you share certain text-based files (.pdf, .docx, .pptx, and .xlsx) in channels or DMs, Slack will automatically summarize the file.

Summaries are only available for files that are accessible to everyone and will appear below a file with a Summarize icon. To view a more detailed summary, hover over a file and select View summary . To translate a file summary into your default translation language , click Translate .

section.title: Manage your file summaries
content: You can decide whether to display file summaries. If you turn file summaries off, they won’t be generated for any files you add to Slack, and you won’t see summaries for others’ files.

From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Click Preferences . Select AI . Below File summaries , choose whether you’d like to summarize files you upload and display summaries for files that other people upload.

images.alt: Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

section.title: Translate messages
content: Use AI to translate messages in Slack written in another language. First, set your translation language, and then select a message to translate.

section.title: Set your translation language
content: From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Click Preferences . Select Language & region . Below Translation language , choose the default language you’d like to translate messages to.

section.title: Translate a message
content: Once you’ve set a translation language, you can translate messages in Slack. Translations are only visible to you, so other people will always see the original message.
Desktop
Mobile

In any conversation, hover over a message. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the message, then select Translate message . Click See original below the translated message to view it in the original language.
In any conversation, long press a message. Tap Translate Message . Tap See original below the translated message to view it in the original language.

section.title: Explain messages
content: If you come across a message that contains lots of acronyms or covers a complex topic, ask AI to explain it. Explanations break messages down to help you understand their meaning and context, and are not visible to anyone else.
Desktop
Mobile

In any conversation, hover over a message. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the message, then select Explain message . Your explanation will open to the right of the message. Click Sources to view any messages and files referenced in the answer, or click Share to forward your explanation to others.
Open any conversation. Long press a message, then tap Explain Message . Your explanation will open below the message. Tap Share to forward it to others.
Tip: You can also get explanations for JPG, PNG, and GIF images up to 4 MB in size and PDFs up to 10 MB in size.

page: Get your work done from the Activity view

section.title: Activity overview
content: When you open Activity, you’ll see a feed of all your recent messages and notifications. Switch between dense view to scan lots of messages at once or detailed view for extra context. Choose a filter to view only certain notifications (like mentions, DMs, and reminders) and create your own saved views to customize your feed. Mark notifications as read so it’s easy to see what you’ve already looked at, or clear them to keep things tidy.

section.title: Switch between detailed and dense layouts
content: There are two views available to you when working from Activity in Slack on desktop — detailed and dense. Detailed layout gives you more context for each notification in the feed, while Dense offers a more traditional inbox-style layout where you can see more entries at once.
From your desktop, click Activity in the sidebar. Select View as detailed or View as dense in the top right corner.

section.title: Filter Activity
content: Each type of notification that appears in Activity has its own filter so you can view only certain items. From the All view on desktop, click Filters to see a complete list:

Unreads All messages and notifications you haven’t read yet. DMs Any direct messages you receive. Mentions Messages where you’ve been mentioned . Threads Replies to threads you’re following and threads you’ve been mentioned in. Channels Messages in channels where your notification preference is set to All new posts . Reactions Messages people reacted to with an emoji . Invitations Notifications about channels you’re added to and new Slack Connect invitations . Apps Notifications from apps , ex. Google Calendar invitations or updates from Jira. Reminders All of your personal reminders . VIP Notifications from your VIPs . Only available on paid plans . Cleared notifications Any notifications you’ve cleared . Specific channel or section Notifications from certain channels or sidebar sections . Only available on paid plans .

section.title: Reply to messages and threads
content: Reply to any message or thread from Activity. Messages you reply to will automatically be marked as read, or you can clear the notification from your feed.
Desktop
Mobile

Click Activity in the sidebar. Select a message to reply, or hover over a message and click the three dots icon to view additional options like opening it in a channel or DM, setting a reminder, or turning off thread reply notifications.
Tap Activity at the bottom of the screen. Tap a message to reply, or long press a message to view additional options like setting a reminder or turning off thread reply notifications.

section.title: Clear notifications
content: To keep Activity organized, you can clear any notifications you no longer need in your feed.
Desktop
Mobile
Click Activity in the sidebar. Hover over a message, then click Clear notification . To clear in bulk, check the box next to multiple notifications and select Clear selected notifications .
Tap Activity at the bottom of the screen. Swipe left on a message to clear it.
Tip: On desktop, check the box at the top of your feed to select and clear or mark all notifications as read.

section.title: Create and manage custom views
content: Saved views let you personalize how Activity is organized by preserving custom combinations of filters you can access from tabs at the top of your feed anytime. While you can only create saved views on desktop, you can also access them on mobile.

section.title: Create a custom view
content: From your desktop, click Activity in the sidebar. Click the plus icon at the top of the screen and select Create a custom view . Enter a title for your view. Choose between detailed or dense layout. Click the toggle to only show unreads in your view, then check the box next to the notifications you'd like to include. Select specific channnels or sections from the drop-down menu if you'd like. Click Save .

section.title: Edit a custom view
content: From your desktop, click Activity in the sidebar. Click the plus icon at the top of the screen and select Edit views . Select the view you want to edit, and check or uncheck the boxes for your preferred filters. Click Save .

section.title: Delete a custom view
content: From your desktop, click Activity in the sidebar. Right-click on a custom view and select Delete view . Click Delete .
Tip: Drag and drop tabs at the top of Activity to re-order them.

section.title: View and update Salesforce objects
content: You can view and update Salesforce opportunities in Slack. When you update an opportunity in Slack, it’ll automatically update in Salesforce.
Desktop
Mobile

Click Sales in the sidebar. If you don’t see Sales , click More to find it. Select View Opportunities in the top right. Select an opportunity list, or search for a list in the drop-down menu. Choose an opportunity, then update any fields you'd like.

From the Home tab, tap Sales . Tap Opportunities . Choose a suggested opportunity list, or tap the magnifying glass in the top right to search for a list. Tap on a field to update it, or tap the three dots icon in the top right for more options.

section.title: Add key metrics
content: Use metrics to track your progress towards important sales targets. You can configure up to six metrics to appear in Your insights .
From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar.  If you don’t see Sales , click More to find it. Below Your insights , click Add metric . Add a Salesforce report link, then choose a metric and a name.
Note: You can view key metrics and notifications from the Slack mobile apps, but they can only be set up from Slack on desktop.

section.title: Set up and manage notifications
content: Use notifications to create reminders for yourself to update opportunities, stay informed about important deals, and more. These notifications will appear in the Sales notifications section of Sales Home.

section.title: Create a notification
content: From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar.  If you don’t see Sales , click More to find it. Select Manage notifications . Click Create notification . Choose a template, then customize the notification if you’d like. Click Save Notification .

section.title: Delete a notification
content: From your desktop, click Sales in the sidebar.  If you don’t see Sales , click More to find it. Select Manage notifications . Hover over a notification, then click Delete .
Tip: You can also use Workflow Builder to send Sales Home notifications by starting your workflow with a specific event in Salesforce and adding Sales steps.
Who can use this feature?
Sales Admins Available on the new version of Business+ and Enterprise+ plans Available on the Business+ and Enterprise Grid plans with the legacy Slack Sales Elevate add-on

page: Introduce people across the organizations you work with

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: By default, all members (but not guests )

section.title: What to expect
content: You can share someone’s contact info if you’re from the same company or if you work together in a Slack Connect channel or DM. Contact information includes someone's full name, display name , profile picture, email address (depending on their Slack settings), and company name — some of the basic elements you can see in their Slack profile. You won’t be able to share someone’s contact info if they’ve adjusted their contact sharing preferences . To share someone's contact info, you must be using a paid Slack plan , but the person you're sharing contact info with can be using any plan. People will see that you've shared their info if they receive an invitation to connect.

section.title: Share someone’s contact info
content: From your desktop, hover over More . Select External connections , then type the name of the person whose contact info you'd like to share. Click the person's name in the results to open their profile. From the person's profile, click the three dots icon , then select Share contact . Search for the channel or person you'd like to share contact info with, then click Share .
Note: When you share someone's contact information, they can ignore or block any invitations from people they don't want to connect with.

images.alt: An image of a cursor over the More icon in the Slack desktop app.

section.title: Working with contact info
content: Here are the options people will see when they hover over the contact info you've shared:
Send a message Click Message to start a DM conversation . Share contact info Share this person’s contact info if someone else would benefit from reaching out to them.
Note: Depending on each organization's Slack settings, people who are introduced may not be able to message each other in Slack.
By default, all members (but not guests ) Available on paid plans

section.title: Conversations
content: You can open any channel or DM in Slack in a separate window.
From Home , press Cmd (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows/Linux). Click the name of a channel or DM to open it in a window.

section.title: Threads
content: Open a thread in a new window to continue to follow along with a conversation while you navigate to another channel or page in Slack.
From your desktop, open a thread. Click the three dots icon . Select Open in new window .

section.title: Activity and Later tabs
content: To keep Activity or Later open while you navigate between tabs and conversations, you can open it in a new window.
From your desktop, hover over Activity or Later to reveal a preview of the tab. Click the window icon to open it in a window.
Tip: You can also open a separate window by pressing ⌘ (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows) when clicking Activity or Later in your sidebar.

section.title: Canvases
content: To open a canvas in a separate window, use the steps below:
Open the canvas. Click the three dots icon . Select Open in new window .

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: By default, all members and sometimes guests

section.title: What to expect
content: @everyone notifies every person in the the general channel , @channel notifies all members of a channel, and @here notifies only the active members of a channel. These mentions won't notify people when their notifications are paused , or when they're used in threads . In channels with at least six members, Slack will ask you to confirm before you send a message with any of these mentions . Owners and admins can turn this warning off . In an Enterprise organization, these mentions work differently in channels. If there are 10,000 members or more, only owners and admins can use @channel and @here.

We suggest using these mentions sparingly. If you need to get the attention of someone specific, you can mention that person directly . On the Pro, Business+, and Enterprise plans, you can also notify a specific group of people by creating a user group .

Note: Owners and admins with permission can choose to restrict who can use @everyone, @channel, and @here. If you don’t have the option to notify a channel or workspace, find an owner and ask for help.

section.title: @everyone
content: @everyone can only be used in the general channel , which is a channel that all members (except guests) are automatically added to. This mention will notify everyone in the general channel whether their availability is set to active or away.
When to use @everyone
Give your organization information about a new vacation policy. Alert everyone in the company about an emergency evacuation drill.
Note: By default, guests aren't able to use @everyone.

section.title: @channel
content: Use @channel to let everyone in a channel know about timely, relevant information. This will trigger a desktop or mobile notification for all members of the channel, whether their availability is set to active or away.
When to use @channel
Update your team about a last-minute change to a project deadline. Let members know when you adjust a work process or the channel structure.
Tip: If you're building a Slack app that can notify members, the message from your app's bot user must contain <!channel> or <!everyone>.

section.title: @here
content: Use @here when you only need the attention of people who are actively working in any channel you’re a member of. This is great for when you don’t want to notify coworkers who aren’t available at the time.
When to use @here
Schedule an impromptu event for people who are available, like a lunch outing. Get a question answered quickly by coworkers who are on Slack.
By default, all members and sometimes guests Available on all plans

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Workspace Owners / Admins can create and edit workspace-level user groups by default, but they can make this feature available to all members
Org Owners / Admins can create and edit org-level user groups

section.title: Create a user group for your workspace
content: Workspace Owners and Admins can manage permissions for workspace-level user groups . If you don’t see the option to create user groups, an admin has restricted access to this feature. Use these steps to create a user group that is unique to your workspace.

From the Home tab, click Directories . Click User Groups , then select Create user group . Choose a name and handle for your user group. If you’d like, set a purpose or select default channels for group members to be added to . You can also create a shared sidebar section . When you're ready, click Next . Under Add members , search for and select the members you’d like to add. When you’re done, click Create Group .
Tip: If you're on the Business+ plan, you can use SCIM provisioning to create a workspace-level user group.

section.title: Create a user group for your Enterprise organization
content: Org Owners and Admins on Enterprise plans can create org-level user groups from the admin dashboard. These can be used for permissions and membership across multiple workspaces, similar to IDP groups .

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People , then click Groups . Click Create Group in the top right corner. Add a name for the group and, if you want, add a description. Click Create and Continue to Members . Select the box next to members you want to add to a group, then click Save .
Note: Org-level user groups created by admins in Slack can’t be managed from SCIM provisioning or combined with IDP groups. They also can’t be @ mentioned in a channel.

section.title: Edit a user group
content: Members with permission can make edits to workspace-level user groups. Owners and Admins can manage these permissions as well as additional user group settings in the admin dashboard.

section.title: Add or remove members
content: From the Home tab, click Directories . Click User Groups . Click on a user group, then select Edit Members . Make your changes, the click Save .
Note: Guests and people you work with in Slack Connect channels and DMs can’t be added to user groups in your organization, and they will not be able to mention user groups you create.

section.title: Manage user groups
content: From the Home tab, click Directories. Click User Groups . Click on the user group you'd like to manage, then click the three dots icon . To update your group's name, handle, or default channels, select Edit group details from the menu. Click Save when you're finished. To deactivate your user group, select Deactivate group , then Deactivate to confirm.

Note: If you deactivate a user group, you'll be unable to mention its handle or view its members. The user group won't be deleted from your list of groups, and all members will remain in the group unless removed.
Who can use this feature?

Workspace Owners / Admins can create and edit workspace-level user groups by default, but they can make this feature available to all members Org Owners / Admins can create and edit org-level user groups Available on paid plans

page: Add custom emoji and aliases to your workspace

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: By default, all members but not guests

section.title: Custom emoji
content: Custom emoji are available for everyone in your organization to use and can be accessed from the Slack icon in the emoji picker.

section.title: Add custom emoji
content: Square images under 128KB and with transparent backgrounds work best. Images can be in JPG, PNG, or GIF format.  GIFs can include up to  50 frames.
Desktop
iOS

From your desktop, click the smiley face icon in the message field to open the emoji menu. Click Add Emoji . Click Upload Image and select a file. Under Give it a name , enter a name for your emoji, then click Save .

Tap the smiley face icon in the message field to open the menu. Enter a name for your custom emoji, then tap Add custom emoji . If your emoji name is taken, choose another. Select an option and follow the prompts to upload an image. When you’re ready, tap Add in the top right corner.
Note: It's not currently possible to add custom emoji from the Slack Android app.
Tip: When working in a Slack Connect channel or direct message, you can right-click another organization’s custom emoji to add it to your organization.

images.alt: Emoji menu showing frequently used emoji and button to add new ones

section.title: Remove custom emoji
content: Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins (free, Pro, and Business+ plans) and Org Owners and Org Admins (Enterprise Grid plan) can delete any custom emoji. Members can only delete emoji they’ve added.

From your desktop, click your workspace name in the top left. Select Customize [workspace name] . If you're an owner or admin, you'll need to click Settings & administration first. Click the Emoji tab at the top of the page. Search for the emoji you'd like to remove, then click the delete icon . Select Delete Emoji to confirm.

section.title: Emoji packs
content: An emoji pack is a set of custom emoji created just for Slack that you can add to your workspace. Like other custom emoji, emoji packs will appear can be accessed from the Slack icon in the emoji picker.

section.title: Add an emoji pack
content: Owners, admins, and members with permission can add an emoji pack.
From your desktop, click the smiley face icon in the message field to open the emoji menu. Click Add Emoji Click the Emoji packs tab at the top of the page. Select an emoji pack. Click Add Pack .

section.title: Remove an emoji pack
content: Owners and admins can remove an emoji pack.

From your desktop, click the smiley face icon in the message field to open the emoji menu. Click Add Emoji . Click the Emoji packs tab at the top of the page. Select the emoji pack you’d like to remove. Click Remove Pack .
Note: It’s not possible to remove individual emoji from an emoji pack.

section.title: Emoji aliases
content: Emoji aliases let you add your own emoji codes to Slack. If you have trouble remembering certain emoji codes, adding an alias can make it easier to find and use these emoji in Slack.

section.title: Create an emoji alias
content: From your desktop, click your workspace name in the top left. Select Customize [workspace name] . If you're an owner or admin, you'll need to click Settings & administration first. Select Add Alias , then click Choose Emoji . Choose an emoji from the drop-down menu. Under Enter an alias , enter the new code you'd like to use. Select Save .
Note: Members with permission to delete custom emoji can delete emoji aliases they've added. Owners and admins can delete any emoji alias.
By default, all members but not guests Available on all plans

section.title: Star a channel or DM
content: Desktop
Mobile
Open a channel or DM. Click the star icon at the top of the conversation. If you've organized your sidebar with custom sections , then click Starred from the menu.
Open the channel or DM you'd like to star. Tap the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header. Tap the three dots icon in the top-right corner, then tap Move to starred .
Note: To remove a conversation from your Starred section, use the same steps above.

page: Save messages and files for later

section.title: Save a message or file
content: Desktop
Mobile

section.title: Save a message
content: Hover over the message you'd like to save. Click the save icon .

section.title: Save a file
content: Hover over the file you'd like to save. Click the More actions icon . Select Save for Later .

section.title: Save a message
content: Tap the message you’d like to save. Tap the save icon .

section.title: Save a file
content: Tap the file you’d like to save. Tap the three dots icon . Select Save for Later .
Note: Saving a file keeps it accessible in Slack, but you can also download a file to your device to keep a copy elsewhere.

section.title: View your saved items
content: Your saved items will be organized into three separate tabs within Later :

In progress In progress is where you’ll find your reminders and newly saved items. From here, you can jump to the messages and files in their original conversations, archive them, mark them as complete, or set a date and time to receive a reminder. Archived Archived is the place to store a message or file you’ll need down the road. It could be something you reference often, or something that doesn’t have a task associated with it but is still handy to keep around. Completed When you’re done with a saved message or file, you can mark it as complete to check it off your to-do list. Anything you mark as complete will be moved to Completed in case you need to come back to it later.
Tip: Move completed items back to In progress by clicking the three dots icon and selecting Move to In progress.
To view your saved items, follow the steps below:
Desktop
Mobile
Click Later . Switch between In progress , Archived , or Completed to see all your saved items.
Tap Home . Tap Later . Switch between In progress , Archived , or Completed to see all your saved items.

section.title: Jump to a saved item
content: Desktop
Mobile
From In progress , Archived , or Completed , find the item you'd like to open. In the top-right corner of the message or file, click the Open in Home .
From the In progress , Archived , or Completed tab, tap a message or file to open it.

section.title: Archive a saved item
content: Desktop
Mobile
From In progress , click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the message or file you’d like to move, then select Archive .
From the In progress tab, long press the message or file you’d like to archive. Tap Archive .

section.title: Mark a saved item as complete
content: Desktop
Mobile
From In progress , click the Complete icon in the top-right corner of the message or file you’d like to mark as complete.
From the In progress tab, find the item you'd like to mark as complete, then tap the Complete button .

section.title: Set or edit a reminder
content: You can set a reminder for messages or files you’ve saved so that you’ll be notified to come back to them at a later time.
Desktop
Mobile
From In progress , click the reminder icon in the top-right of the message or file you’d like to be reminded of. Select a time from the list, or set a Custom date and time and click Update.
From the In progress tab, find the item you’d like to set a reminder for, then tap the reminder icon . Select a time from the list, or set a Custom date and time and click Set Reminder.
Any reminder you set from the More actions menu on a message will also appear in In progress , where you’ll be able to mark it as complete or edit the timeframe by following the steps above.

section.title: Filter upcoming reminders
content: By default, In progress will show all your upcoming and past-due reminders alongside other items you’ve saved. If you’d like, you can filter out upcoming reminders so that you can focus on the ones that are currently due:
From In progress on desktop, click the filter icon in the top right. Select Show upcoming reminders to show or hide them from the list of saved items and reminders.
Tip: Create additional filter views for reminders in Activity .

section.title: Remove a message or file from Later
content: Desktop
Mobile
Click Later . Hover over the message, reminder or file you’d like to remove from your saved items. Click the save icon .
Tap Home . Tap Later . Press and hold the message or file you’d like to remove from your saved items. Select Remove from Later .

section.title: Start or reply to a thread
content: Desktop
Mobile

Hover over the message you'd like to reply to. Click the Reply in thread icon . Type your reply. If you'd like to send your reply back to the channel or DM's main view, check the box below your message. Send your message.

Tap the message you’d like to reply to. Tap Reply in Thread , or tap the Add a reply field to add to an existing thread. Type your reply. If you'd like to send your reply back to the channel or DM's main view, check the box below your message. Tap the paper plane icon to send your message.
Note: You can also send a reply back to the channel after you've sent it. Click the three dots icon (on desktop) or tap and hold the thread reply (on mobile) and select Send reply to this channel .

images.alt: A thread to keep discussion organized in Slack

section.title: Open threads in a new window
content: From Slack on desktop, you can open any thread in a window to view it alongside any other conversation.
From a channel or DM, open a thread. In the top right corner, click the window icon .

section.title: Manage thread notifications
content: By default, you’ll be notified of new replies to all threads in one-to-one DMs . In channels or DMs with multiple people, you'll be notified of new replies if you started the thread, replied to it, or were mentioned .

section.title: Manage notifications for a single thread
content: Desktop
Mobile
Hover over the thread. Click the three dots icon . Select Get notified about new replies or Turn off notifications for replies .

Tap the thread. Tap the three dots icon below the original message. Select Get Notified about New Replies to receive notifications for all new thread replies, or Turn Off Notifications for Replies to stop receiving notifications.

section.title: Get notifications for all threads in a channel
content: From your desktop, open a channel you’d like to adjust notifications for and click the channel name in the conversation header. Below the channel name, click the notifications menu. Select More notification options . Check the box next to Get notified about all replies and show them in your Threads view . Click Save Changes .

section.title: View all threads
content: Desktop
Mobile
From Home , click Threads to view threads you are a part of. Threads with unread replies will appear at the top of the list. Click a thread to open it and send a reply.
You can also hover over a thread for additional options:
Add an emoji reaction Open the thread in a channel or direct message Save a message for later Access more options, like turning off notifications for a thread

From Home , tap Threads at the top of your screen to see all the conversations you're following. Threads with unread replies will appear at the top of the list. From your Threads view, you can do the following:
Reply to any thread Select a thread to open it in the original conversation Unfollow a thread if you'd no longer like to be notified of new replies
Tip: When you've read a thread reply that you’d like to come back to later, you can mark the message as unread .
Who can use this feature?
All members and guests Available on all plans

section.title: How to send email to Slack
Create an email address for a channel or DM
content: By default, anyone can create an email address for a channel or DM. Once an email address has been created for a conversation, anyone with the email address can use it to send email to Slack.
Note: If you work with people from other organizations in channels , each organization can create a unique email address for a channel. Any email sent to that channel will be visible to all members.

section.title: Create an email address
content: From your desktop, open the channel or DM you’d like to send email to. Click the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header. Click the Integrations tab. Select Send emails to this [channel] or [conversation] . Click Get Email Address . If you’d like to set up an automatic forwarding rule from your email provider or add the email to your address book, click Copy next to the email address. If you created an email address for a channel, Slackbot will post a message that’s only visible to you with a prompt to let members know an email address has been created. Click Share Email Address to post a message to the channel with any details you’d like. Otherwise, click Dismiss .
Note: Owners and admins can manage members’ ability to create email addresses for channels and DMs. If you don’t see this option, find an owner or admin to ask for help.

images.alt: Gif of a cursor clicking the channel name in the channel header

section.title: Customize email appearance
content: If you’d like, you can add an image and custom name for emails posted to Slack so they’re easier for people to recognize.

From your desktop, open a channel or DM with an email address. Click the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header. Click the Integrations tab. Select Send emails to this [channel] or [conversation] . Click Customize Email Appearance . Below Email Icon , open the drop-down menu to upload an image or choose an emoji to display alongside emails posted to Slack. Below Email Name , enter a label for your emails. Click Save Changes .

section.title: Delete an email address
content: Owners, admins, and members with permission to create email addresses for conversations can delete the email address for any channel or DM they’re a part of. If a conversation’s email address is deleted, emails sent to it will not be posted in Slack.

From your desktop, open the channel or DM. Click the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header. Click the Integrations tab. Select Send emails to this [channel] or [conversation] . Below the email address, click Delete Address . Click Delete email address to confirm.

section.title: Use an email add-on
content: Gmail
Outlook

section.title: Send email to Slack
content: Head to the Slack for Gmail page in the Google Workspace Marketplace to install the Slack add-on to Gmail. If you’re unable to install the add-on, ask a Google Workspace administrator at your company to approve Slack for Gmail from the Google Workspace Admin Console. After you install the add-on, click the Slack icon in the right sidebar to connect your Gmail account to Slack. When prompted, open an email and click Connect to Slack . To send an email to Slack, click the Slack icon in the right sidebar and select Search Channels and People . Choose a workspace from the drop-down menu, then type the name of a channel or person and press Enter or select their name . Click Send to [name] . Click View to see your email in Slack.

section.title: Disconnect Gmail and Slack
content: Head to the Google Workspace Marketplace . Click the gear icon in the top-right corner, then select Manage Apps . Find Slack, then click Manage . Click Remove .
Tip: If you don’t use Google Workspace, you can remove the add-on from the Add-ons section of your Gmail settings.

section.title: What to expect
content: The Outlook email add-in is only available for Office 365. It’s not supported for on-premise Microsoft Exchange customers. Only the Exchange mail protocol is supported, so you won’t be able to use the add-in if your Outlook client is set up to receive messages with POP/IMAP. On-premises SharePoint installations or Office 365 plans hosted on a Microsoft national cloud deployment (including Office 365 U.S. Government, Office 365 Germany, and Office 365 operated by 21Vianet in China) are not currently supported.

section.title: Send email to Slack
content: Head to the Slack for Outlook page in Microsoft AppSource. Click Get it now and follow the prompts. If you’re unable to install the add-in yourself, contact an Office 365 administrator at your company for help. After you install the add-in, connect Outlook to your Slack workspace. If you use the Outlook desktop app, click the Slack icon in the toolbar and select Connect to Slack . If you use Outlook in a browser, open an email and click the three dots icon , then select Slack for Outlook . To send an email to Slack from the Outlook desktop app, open an email and click the Slack icon to select the name of a channel or person from the dropdown menu. Click Send to Slack to send the email. To send an email to Slack from Outlook in a browser, open an email and click the three dots icon and select Send to Slack . Select the name of a channel or person from the dropdown menu, then click Send to Slack .
Note: If you run into problems connecting Slack and Outlook, try using Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox , then restart the Outlook desktop app.

section.title: Disconnect Outlook and Slack
content: Sign in to the Outlook desktop app. Click Get add-ins from the toolbar. Click My add-ins . Find Slack for Outlook and click the three dots icon . Click Remove .

section.title: Set up a Slackbot forwarding address
content: From your desktop, click your profile picture in the tab bar. Select Preferences from the menu. Click Messages & media . Scroll down to Bring emails into Slack , then click Get a Forwarding Address . Slack will generate a forwarding email address. Click Copy and use the forwarding address to set up a forwarding rule in your email client if you’d like.
If you need to stop forwarding emails, go to the Messages & media section of your preferences. Below your forwarding address, click Disable this address .
Note: If emails you send to Slack aren’t delivered, incoming emails may have been disabled for your workspace or org. Find an owner or admin to ask for help.
Who can use this feature?
All members (by default) Available on all plans

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: All members , but guests can only set reminders for themselves.

section.title: Create reminders
content: When you set yourself a reminder, you’ll receive a notification and see a badge on the Later and Activity tabs when the date and time arrives.

section.title: Create a personal reminder
content: Desktop
Mobile
Click the Later tab in your sidebar. Click the plus sign at the top-right corner of the list. Select a date and time for your reminder. Enter the details of your reminder, then click Save .
From the Home tab, tap the plus sign . Select a date and time for your reminder. Enter the details of your reminder, then tap Save .

section.title: Create a reminder from a message or a file
content: Desktop
Mobile

In any conversation, hover over a message or file. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the message or file, then select Remind me about this . Choose a time from the list, or select Custom time to pick your own.
In any conversation, tap and hold a message or file. Tap Remind me . Choose a time from the list, or select Custom time to pick your own.

section.title: Create a reminder from an item in a list
content: From a list, hover over an item and click Open . Click the three dots icon , then select Remind me about this . Choose a time, or select Custom time to pick your own.

section.title: Create a reminder from a date in a canvas
content: In any canvas, start typing a date. You can write it as a day ("tomorrow" or "Tuesday"), a date (December 31st), or in month/day/year format (12/31/2024). Select the date to add it to the canvas. Hover over the date, then click Add reminder . Choose a time, or select Custom time to pick your own.
Note: Setting reminders in a canvas or a list is available only on desktop.

section.title: Create a channel reminder
content: When you set a channel reminder, Slack will send a message to the channel with the reminder description at your chosen date and time. Channel reminders work best for simple team reminders. For more complex messages, we recommend creating a workflow using the scheduled message template .
Desktop
Mobile

Type /remind in the message field and select it from the shortcuts menu . In the message field, enter the details of your reminder following this format: /remind [#channel] [what] [when] . Ex.: /remind #marketing-team to submit expenses every Thursday. Send your message to schedule the reminder.

From a channel or DM, tap the message field. In the message field, enter the details of your reminder following this format: /remind [#channel] [what] [when] . Ex.: /remind #marketing-team to submit expenses every Thursday. Send your message to schedule the reminder.

Note: You can set reminders to repeat by the day (ex., every Monday) but not in time increments (ex., every hour). For the best experience, we recommend using the American English date and time format.

section.title: Personal reminders
content: You can complete reminders you set for yourself, edit them, or delete them from the Later tab .
Desktop
Mobile

Click Later in the sidebar. From the In progress tab, hover over a reminder. To mark a reminder complete, click the checkmark icon . To edit a reminder, click the clock icon , then select a new reminder due date. To delete a reminder, click the three dots icon , then select Delete reminder .
Tap Later at the top of your mobile app. From the In progress tab, tap Complete , or tap the reschedule icon to edit your reminder. To delete a reminder, tap and hold it, then tap Remove from Later .

section.title: Channel reminders
content: Channel reminders can’t be edited, but you can delete and recreate them if you need to. To delete a channel reminder, follow the steps below in the channel where Slack sends the reminder message.
Desktop
Mobile

Type /remind list in the message field, then send your message. A message that is only visible to you will appear, showing you the channel reminders you can delete. Find the reminder in the list, then click Delete .

Tap the message field. Type /remind list , then send your message. A message that is only visible to you will appear, showing you the channel reminders you can delete. Find the reminder in the list, then tap Delete .

section.title: Set a default reminder time
content: By default, reminders you set for a specific day (like “tomorrow” or “every Tuesday”) will be delivered at 9 a.m. in your time zone. If you’d like, you can adjust this:

From your desktop, click your profile picture in the sidebar. Select Preferences from the menu. Under Set a default time for reminder notifications ,
        select an option from the drop-down menu.
Who can use this feature?
All members , but guests can only set reminders for themselves. Available on all plans

images.alt: Static image of a cursor clicking the profile picture menu in the Slack app

section.title: View your unread messages
content: Desktop
Mobile
From Home , click Unreads at the top of your sidebar. If you don't see this option, you can adjust your sidebar preferences to always show Unreads in your sidebar.
From Home , tap Catch up . You’ll see a preview of your most recent unread message, and a count of how many unread messages are available to swipe through.

section.title: Sort and filter unread conversations
content: Change how your unreads are sorted on your desktop to best suit your working style. Click the Sort menu at the top of the Unreads view to sort messages like your sidebar, alphabetically, in a recommended order, by newest activity, or by oldest activity.

You can filter your unread conversations according to your sidebar sections . To filter, click the Filter menu, right next to Sort . On paid plans , you'll be able to filter by each of your custom sidebar sections .
Note: Sorting and filtering options for unread messages are only available on desktop.

section.title: Mark messages as read
content: Desktop
Mobile
Click Mark as Read to clear a conversation's messages when you've read them. You can also scroll to the bottom of the Unreads view and click Mark All Messages Read .

If you clicked Mark as Read too quickly, click Undo to restore the messages to the Unreads view. When you’d like to come back to a conversation's messages later, click the arrow icon beside the conversation name to collapse it. Click the icon again when you're ready to view the unread messages.
From the message preview, swipe right to mark a conversation’s messages as read and move on to the next unread message. You can also press and hold the Mark as Read button to mark all messages read.
If you swiped on a conversation too quickly, tap Undo to view the messages again. To leave a message unread and come back to it later, swipe left to skip it.

section.title: Refresh for new messages
content: Desktop
Mobile
When new messages become available while you’re viewing your Unreads , the syncing arrows icon will appear in the header. Click the icon to reveal a fresh batch of unread messages.
To see new unread messages, you'll need to reopen the Catch up view. Tap the close icon , then tap Catch up to reopen it.

section.title: Reply in a conversation
content: Desktop
Mobile
To send a message in an unread channel or DM, or to jump to a conversation, click the timestamp on any message.
To send a message in an unread channel or DM, type your reply in the message field. To jump to a conversation, tap an unread message, then tap the conversation name at the top.

section.title: Message actions
content: Desktop
Mobile
You can't send new messages from the Unreads view, but you can hover on any message, then click the three dots icon to save , share , add a reaction , pin , set a reminder , start a thread and more.
Tap and hold any message in the Catch up view to access the message actions, where you can add a reaction , set a reminder , save for later , forward , and more.

section.title: Keyboard shortcuts
content: Use these shortcuts on your desktop to get caught up even faster from the Unreads view.
Tip: To view a list of keyboard shortcuts, press ⌘ + / (Mac) or Ctrl + / (Windows/Linux) or visit Slack keyboard shortcuts .

page: Edit message retention settings for specific conversations

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Workspace Owners and Org Owners can make this feature available to all members

section.title: What to expect
content: If member overrides are allowed , members can set their own retention period for private channels and DMs. Owners will be able to adjust this for public channels as well. If admin overrides are allowed , owners and admins on the Business+ and Enterprise plans can set message retention for channels using channel management tools . In channels shared with external organizations , retention settings will only apply to the messages sent by members of your organization. In an Enterprise org, multi-workspace channels will always adhere to the organization retention policy. In cases where the org-level policy isn't set, the default is to keep all messages.
Caution! Message deletion is permanent. Please use care when setting up retention policies.

section.title: Set message retention for a specific channel or DM
content: From your desktop, open the conversation you'd like to configure retention settings for. Click the channel or member name(s) in the conversation header. Click the Settings tab. Hover over Message history and click Edit . Select Delete messages after a specific time period . Choose how long you'd like to save messages, then click Save Changes .
Slack will post a message to the conversation to confirm the updated retention settings.

section.title: Set message retention with channel management tools
content: Business+ plan
Enterprise plans

Workspace Owners and Admins can use channel management tools to view and adjust message retention on public channels. The Workspace Primary Owner, and owners and admins with permission , can also take this action on private channels.

From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace settings . Below Administration in the left sidebar, select Manage channels . If you don’t see the left sidebar, click Menu in the top-left corner to find it. Search for a channel name, or filter channels by channel type. If you have permission to manage private channels, you can check the box next to Show all private channels . To set or change retention on a channel, click the three dots icon to the right of the channel name and select Edit message history . Make and save your changes.
Slack will post a message to the channel to let members know that retention was updated and which owner or admin took the action.
Note: On the Business+ plan, you can only edit retention on private channels if a request to export data from all channels and conversations has been approved for your workspace.

section.title: Org level
content: The Org Primary Owner, and any Org Owners or Org Admins with permission, can use the steps below to view and edit message retention on channels in their org:

From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . Click Channels in the left sidebar. Search for a channel name, or filter channels by channel type or workspace. If you have permission to manage private channels, you can check the box next to Show all private channels . To set or change retention on a channel, click the three dots icon to the right of the channel name and select Edit message history. Make and save your changes.
Slack will post a message to the channel to let members know that retention was updated and which owner or admin took the action.

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Owners and Admins can use the steps below to view and edit message retention on channels in workspaces they manage:

From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace settings . (If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.) Below Administration in the left sidebar, select Manage channels . If you don’t see the left sidebar, click Menu in the top-left corner to find it. Search for a channel name, or filter channels by channel type. If you have permission to manage private channels, you can check the box next to Show all private channels . To set or change retention on a channel, click the three dots icon to the right of the channel name and select Edit message history . Make and save your changes.
Slack will post a message to the channel to let members know that retention was updated and which owner or admin took the action.
Workspace Owners and Org Owners can make this feature available to all members Available on paid plans

page: Use AI to write or edit content in a canvas

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Available on the new version of Business+ and Enterprise+ plans
Available on the Pro , Business+ , and Enterprise Grid plans with the legacy Slack AI add-on

section.title: How it works
content: A blank canvas now has all the context you do in Slack. When creating or editing content, AI can draw from conversations and files you have access to in Slack to include relevant information and convey your message clearly. Describe what you want AI to help write, or choose a prompt from the list to get started even more quickly. Security and integrity are at the core of the canvas AI writing experience. You can expect the same level of privacy and security as other AI features in Slack, and there are guardrails in place to prevent misuse.

section.title: Create a canvas
content: Describe what you want AI to write in your own words, or choose and customize a prompt. If you select a prompt, you may be asked to provide additional information before AI gets to work.

section.title: Start with a prompt
content: The key to creating a good prompt is in the details you add and how specific you are. For example, “Draft an overview of the Acme Corp. conference for the Marketing team using information from #2025-conference and #conference-presentations” will result in a better draft than “Write an update about the Acme Corp. conference.”

From the Home tab, click Files in your sidebar. If you don’t see this option, click More to find it. Click New in the top-right corner and choose New canvas . Select Write with AI . Write a short description of the content you’d like to generate, or choose a prompt from the list. If you’re writing your own prompt, please note that canvas AI is not able to access content from URLs. Depending on the prompt you add or select, you may need to add more detail. For example, to draft a meeting agenda, it’s helpful for Slack to know which channel it will take place in, who will attend, etc. Click Send to generate the content.

section.title: Review and approve
content: Slack will generate content in response to your prompt. More complex prompts may take a few minutes, whereas simpler content will be generated more quickly. You can also use AI to edit content you’ve already written or add sections to an existing canvas. Here’s what to expect:

New content added to your canvas will be highlighted in blue, and formatting like headings, bold and italic text, bullet points, will be applied automatically. Review the content, and click through to view any sources used. Messages will be linked with a number in brackets, and files (like other canvases, lists, or third-party files from connected enterprise search data sources ) will include the type of file alongside the source link. Click Sources to view a complete list. To save the content, click Keep . To start fresh, click Discard . If you’d like to keep the structure and existing content but make some changes, describe them in the Any changes? text field and press Enter .
Tip: If you navigate away from your canvas before clicking Keep to save the content, you can find it at the top of the Recently viewed section of the Files tab.

section.title: Share your canvas
content: Click Share in the top-right corner. Type the name(s) of the people or channels you’d like to share the canvas with, and choose whether they’ll have Can view or Can edit access. Add a message if you’d like, then click Share . To send the link to others, or embed the canvas in another canvas or document, click Copy Link .
Content in your canvas based on private sources will be visible to people you share it with, but they won’t be able to view the original messages or files linked in citations.

section.title: Edit or refine existing content
content: Once you have a first draft of your canvas, or if you want to edit a canvas you already created, use AI to rewrite and refine.

Open a canvas. Highlight the text you’d like to change, then click Edit with AI . You can choose from the following options: • Use a custom prompt Describe the edits you’d like AI to make in your own words. • Quick edits Ask AI to proofread, make text shorter or longer, change the tone, or translate content into another language. • Create additional content Add a summary, create a checklist of action items, or format content into a table.
Tip: Hover over a section of a canvas and click the sparkles to quickly access AI editing options.

section.title: Why don’t I see the option to write with AI?
content: This feature is available on the new version of Business+ and the Enterprise+ plan, and to any customers who are still using the legacy Slack AI add-on. If you’re on Pro or the old version of the Business+ plan without the add-on, you’ll need to upgrade your workspace .
Additionally, owners and admins can disable access to AI features , so canvas writing assistance may be turned off for your workspace or Enterprise organization.

section.title: What information can be used to create content?
content: When you use AI to write or edit content, it can draw from all of the messages and files in Slack that you have access to. If you’re on the Enterprise+ plan, you may also see information from connected enterprise search data sources like Google Drive or Asana. The LLMs used for this feature also have general knowledge, so you may see information added to your canvas that does not have a source. Content derived from messages or files in Slack will always have a source so you can see the original information.

section.title: Which canvas formatting options aren't supported?
content: It’s not currently possible for AI to format content into profile cards, message cards, or column layout.
Who can use this feature?
All members and guests (by default) Available on the new version of Business+ and Enterprise+ plans Available on the Pro , Business+ , and Enterprise Grid plans with the legacy Slack AI add-on

page: Create and share custom list templates

section.title: How it works
content: Create a list, then convert it to a template . Any items in the list will populate the template, so you may want to remove any that don’t work as example items. Share your template with others in your workspace or org so they can use it.
Note: It’s not currently possible to create, share, or use list templates on the Slack mobile apps.

section.title: Create a custom list template
content: To create a custom template, you’ll need to convert an existing list. Once you convert the list to a template, you’ll be able to search for it anytime you need to use it.
From a list, click the three dots icon , then select Convert to a template . Click Convert to Template .

section.title: Share a list template
content: When you convert a list to a template, only people with the link can access it. You can adjust your template’s access permissions to allow more people in your workspace or Enterprise org to use or edit it.

From a list template, click Share in the top-right corner. To manage access for your whole workspace or org, click Only invited people can access and select Anyone in [organization] can view or Anyone in [organization] can edit . Once the changes are saved, the updated version will be available immediately. • Those with Can view access can use your template to create a list. • Those with Can edit access can use and make changes to the template. To manage access for certain people or channels, search for and select their names. Click the drop-down menu next to a person or channel and select Can view or Can edit to decide how the template should be shared, then click Share .
Tip: To prevent people with Can edit access to your template from sharing it with others, follow the steps in Manage list sharing settings .

section.title: Edit a list template
content: You, and anyone else with Can edit access, can edit a list template.

From your desktop, click Files in the sidebar. Click Lists . Next to Templates , select See all . Search for or select the template you’d like to edit. Make your changes. Edits will be saved automatically.

section.title: Revert a template to a list
content: Anyone with Can edit access can revert a template to a list so that it’s no longer available for use as a template.
From the list template, click the three dots icon , then select Revert template to a list . Click Revert to List to confirm.
Who can use this feature?
All members (by default) Available on paid plans

section.title: Print a canvas
content: From your desktop, open the canvas you’d like to print. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner. Select Print canvas . Review the print settings in the system dialog, then click Print .

section.title: Create a PDF
content: You can use your computer’s print settings to save a canvas as a PDF.
Mac
Windows

From your desktop, open the canvas you’d like to print. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner. Select Print canvas . Click PDF in the bottom-left corner of the system dialog. Enter a name for your canvas, then click Save .

From your desktop, open the canvas you’d like to print. Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner. Select Print canvas . Click the Printer drop-down menu on the system dialog, then select Microsoft Print to PDF . Click Print . Enter a name for the PDF of your canvas, then click Save .

images.alt: Display of a Print Dialog modal
Display of a Print Dialog modal

section.title: Create a PDF with active links
content: On the Slack desktop app, links in a canvas will break when you save it as a PDF. To create a PDF with active links, open Slack in a web browser, then follow the steps to create a PDF. Here's how you can open Slack in a web browser:

From the Home tab, click your workspace name in the sidebar, and locate your Slack URL . Open any web browser, then enter your URL. If prompted to sign in, enter your email address and click Sign In with Email . Check your email for a confirmation code from Slack and enter it. In the Open Slack.app pop-up, click Cancel . Click Use Slack in your browser . Create a PDF of a canvas .

section.title: I don’t see the option to print a canvas
content: You can only print canvases that were created by members of your workspace or Enterprise organization. If you don’t see the option to print, the canvas may have been shared by an external person in a Slack Connect conversation, or an owner or admin may have disabled the option to print canvases .

section.title: Content in my canvas is cut off
content: Tables or lists in your canvas that are wider than the dimensions of a page will be cut off when printing or saving as a PDF. Using the print settings in your computer’s system dialog, you can try changing the page orientation from portrait to landscape, changing the paper size, or scaling the content to adjust the fit.

section.title: Add files
content: You can add files up to 1GB in size.
Desktop
Mobile

Drag and drop up to 10 files into the Slack message field, or click the plus icon next to the message field and choose files to add. If you'd like, you can include a message, drag and drop the file previews to reorder them, and if you're adding an image, you can also include a description . Send the message.

Open a channel or direct message (DM). Tap the plus icon next to the message field. To add a photo, tap a recent image or View library . To add a file, tap Recent files or Upload file . Add a message about your file(s) if you'd like. Tap the paper plane icon to send.

Slack will include a preview of a file as part of your message. If you share an image, the preview will only display inline if it's smaller than 25,000 pixels on the longest side, and less than 45 million pixels total. Microsoft Office files that are larger than 50 MB will not display a preview.
Note: Files you add to Slack will be scanned for viruses and other malware, and won't be uploaded if any are detected. If we incorrectly block a file upload, contact us and we can help.

section.title: All files in Slack
content: You can browse files added to any public channels, plus the private channels and direct messages (DMs) you're a part of.
Desktop
Mobile

Click Files in your sidebar. If you don't see this option, click More to find it. Browse your recently viewed files, or select Canvases or Lists in the left sidebar. To filter by file type (like documents or PDFs), click the Types drop-down menu below the search bar.
Tap Search . Tap Files to browse your recently viewed files.
Tip: Press Cmd (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows/Linux) and click to open the Files browser in a new window .

section.title: Files in a channel or DM
content: Open the Files tab in any channel or DM to view all of the files shared in a conversation.
From your desktop, open a channel or DM. Click the Files tab at the top of the conversation. Search for a file, or browse the images, videos, and files shared in the channel or DM.

section.title: Share files

section.title: Share files in Slack

Mobile
Hover over the file you'd like to share. Click the Share icon . Choose where to share the file and add a message, if you'd like. Click Share .

section.title: Share files outside of Slack

Create an external link
Revoke an external link

Mobile

section.title: Find and use canvas templates
