To view details about an upcoming event, like the location, guest list, and description, click the three dots icon to the right and select View event details . Open the app's Messages tab to respond to events or update responses.

From the Google Calendar app's Home tab at the top of the screen, tap Today , Tomorrow , or Select a date to see all events for a particular date. To view details about an upcoming event, like the location, guest list, and description, tap More to the right, then View event details . Open the app's Messages tab to respond to events or update event responses.

Tip: On paid plans , you can receive a daily schedule notification from Google Calendar. Open the app's Home tab, then click Settings to enable or disable your daily schedule, or to change the delivery time.

section.title: Automatically update your Slack status
content: Using your calendar, the Google Calendar app will automatically set your Slack status to In a meeting or Out of Office , to help your coworkers know when to expect a reply from you.

Your status will update to Out of Office when the title of your event contains OOO or PTO , and to In a meeting when the event has other invitees. Your status will not include the name of the meeting you're attending. You can remove or update your status at any time — the Google Calendar app won't override any status you've set yourself. Only the events you accept, or that mark your availability as Busy , will trigger a status update in Slack. If there are overlapping events on your calendar, the Google Calendar app will not update your status.
Note: To manage status syncing, open the app's Home tab, then select Settings to turn Status Sync on or off.

images.alt: A Slack status that reads, In a meeting - Google Calendar app

section.title: Disconnect a calendar
content: Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Google Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Settings . Below the calendar you want to disconnect, click Disconnect Calendar . Click Yes to confirm.

From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Google Calendar. Tap Google Calendar . From the app's Home tab, tap Settings . Below your calendar, tap Disconnect Calendar . Tap Yes to confirm.
Note: If your organization uses domain-wide authentication , you can disconnect your calendars but you won't be able to disconnect your Google account from Slack.

section.title: Fix calendar syncing issues
content: If events are missing or out of date in the Google Calendar app, following the steps below may resolve the problem:
Visit the Google Calendar page in the Slack Marketplace. Click the Configuration tab. Below Your Authorization , click Revoke . After the page reloads, click Add to Slack to reconnect your calendar.

section.title: What's new
content: Salesforce has built a suite of Salesforce for Slack Integrations that can be used alone, or in combination with each other and the Salesforce for Slack app. Installing the Salesforce for Slack app isn’t required, but we recommend it to ensure that all your Salesforce apps can interact, and to simplify authentication and administration with one sign-in for all your apps.
To learn more about which Salesforce for Slack Integrations will best suit your needs, or to get support for the integrations installed in your Slack workspace, visit the Salesforce Help Portal .

section.title: The Salesforce app - built by Slack (legacy)
content: Note: The below information is intended only for reference, as it applies to the now-unsupported Slack-built Salesforce app . If you still have this app installed, switch to the Salesforce built integrations for the best experience.

section.title: The setup
content: Using the Salesforce app requires two apps that connect Salesforce and Slack. Each app provides different functionality:
Previously available in Salesforce AppExchange View Slack messages associated with a record Send Salesforce records to Slack Set up record alerts in Slack channels
Previously available in the Slack Marketplace View Salesforce records for standard objects and any configured custom objects Route relevant alerts to channels Add Slack messages to Salesforce records
In order to use the Salesforce app in Slack, a Salesforce System Administrator will first need to install and configure the Slack app in Salesforce.

section.title: Install and configure the Slack app for Salesforce
content: Salesforce System Administrators can visit Configure Salesforce for use with Slack to install the Slack package in Salesforce, configure standard and custom objects, set user permissions, and more. Once that’s complete, members can follow the steps below to install the Salesforce app to Slack or connect their accounts if the app has already been installed to their workspace.
Tip: If you’re on an Enterprise plan, you can install the Salesforce app at the org level and add it to any workspaces that need access to Salesforce from the admin dashboard.

section.title: Install the Salesforce app to Slack
content: Check with a Salesforce System Administrator to make sure the Slack app for Salesforce has been installed and properly configured before installing the Salesforce app to your Slack workspace.

Visit the Salesforce page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . You’ll be taken to the Salesforce app landing page. From there, click Add to Slack . Follow the prompts to authenticate your Salesforce account and finish installing the app.

Tip: Before connecting Slack to your production Salesforce instance, you can test your setup. To do so, click the Connect to a Salesforce sandbox org? link below the Add to Slack button on the app landing page.

section.title: Connect your Salesforce and Slack accounts
content: Once both apps have been installed, connect your Salesforce and Slack accounts.

From the Slack desktop app, click Apps at the top of your left sidebar. If you don't see this option, click More to find it. Search for and select Salesforce. From the app's Home tab, click Connect Account . Once Slack and Salesforce are connected, click Open Slack to return to Slack.
Note: You can also connect Slack and Salesforce by clicking on a Salesforce alert in a channel, then following the prompts to authenticate Slack with your Salesforce account.

section.title: Search and share Salesforce records in Slack
content: By default, the Salesforce app will return search results for six standard Salesforce objects:
Account Case Contact Lead Opportunity Task

You may be able to search for custom objects if your Salesforce System Administrator has configured them in Salesforce. We recommend contacting your System Administrator if you’d like to request access to specific custom objects in Slack.
To search for and share a Salesforce record in Slack, follow the steps below:

Click the plus icon next to the message field. Search for and select Find and share a record from the menu. Below Search records , enter the name of the record you’re looking for (or select it from the drop-down menu). Click View record . Click Share . Choose a conversation from the drop-down menu and click Share . Click Done .

section.title: Set up Salesforce alerts in Slack
content: There are three types of Salesforce alerts you can set up in your workspace:

My Alerts send you a message when records assigned to you change. Channel Alerts send messages to a channel when a single record or object you’ve selected changes. Bulk Alerts send messages to a channel when a certain record type you’ve selected changes.
Note: Salesforce alerts in both public and private channels will appear as messages from you, since the Salesforce app may not have access to all channels in your workspace.

section.title: Manage My Alerts
content: By default, you’ll receive a message from the Salesforce app when a record is assigned to you in Salesforce. To manage other alerts for standard and custom object record changes in Slack, follow the steps below:

From your desktop, click Apps at the top of your left sidebar. If you don’t see this option, click More to find it. Search for and select Salesforce . From the app’s Home tab, click Set Up My Alerts . Check the box next to each alert you’d like to receive. Click Save .

section.title: Set up channel alerts
content: To post Salesforce record changes to a channel in Slack, you can set up a channel alert:

Click the plus icon next to the message field. Search for and select Add/edit alerts for a channel from the menu. Choose a channel from the drop-down menu. Click Add a record . Below Search records , select a record from the drop-down menu. Click View record . Click Add to [channel name] . Check the box next to each alert you’d like to post to the channel. Click Save .
Tip: To set up a channel alert from Salesforce, click the Slack Alerts button from any record and select a channel.

section.title: Set up bulk alerts
content: Create a bulk alert to post updates about all records of a particular type to a channel.

From your desktop, click Apps at the top of your left sidebar. If you don’t see this option, click More to find it. Search for and select Salesforce. From the app’s Home tab, click Add Bulk Alert . Select a channel from the drop-down menu, then click Next . Choose a record type, then click Next . Click Add to [channel name] . Uncheck the box next to any changes you don’t want to post to the channel as part of your bulk alert. Click Save .

section.title: Troubleshoot alerts
content: If Salesforce alerts you’ve set up stop working, you can disconnect and reconnect your Salesforce account from Slack. Once you’ve reconnected, ask your Salesforce System Administrator to reauthorize your connection to Slack in Salesforce. You can then reconfigure your channel alerts .

Note: Deactivating a member of your workspace will cause any alerts they’ve set to stop working. You’ll need to disconnect and reconnect your Salesforce account in order to restore the missing alerts.

section.title: Send messages to Salesforce or Slack
content: Whether you’re working in Slack or Salesforce, it’s easy to send relevant information between services.

section.title: Send Slack messages to Salesforce
content: Use the Add to Salesforce message shortcut to attach a Slack message to the Related Slack Messages component of any record in Salesforce.
Find the Slack message you’d like to send to Salesforce. Click the three dots icon , then click Add to Salesforce . Search for a record, then select it from the drop-down menu. Click Add .

section.title: Send Salesforce records to Slack
content: Use the Send to Slack action to send records from Salesforce to Slack.

Find the record you'd like to send to Slack. At the top of the page, click the Send to Slack button . Select a workspace, then pick the channel or person you’d like to send the record to. Click Send to Slack .

section.title: Disconnect your account
content: If you no longer want to use the Salesforce app in Slack, you can disconnect your account. This will not uninstall the app from your workspace.

From your desktop, click Apps in the left sidebar. If you don't see this option, click More to find it. Search for and select Salesforce. From the app's Home tab, click Disconnect Account . Click Disconnect to confirm.

page: Configure Salesforce for use with Slack

section.title: Step 1: Set up your custom Salesforce domain
content: To use components in Lightning, your Salesforce org must have a custom domain.

section.title: Register your domain
content: Sign in to Salesforce and open Setup. Using Quick Find in the top left corner of the page, search for My Domain . Enter the domain you'd like to use. Click Check Availability . Once you've found an available domain, click Register Domain . You'll receive an email from Salesforce when registration is complete.

section.title: Deploy your domain to users
content: Open your domain registration email and click the link to sign in to Salesforce. Click Deploy to Users .
Note: Any links to your Salesforce org with your old domain will redirect to the new custom domain automatically.

section.title: Step 2: Install the Slack package to Salesforce
content: Visit the Slack listing in the AppExchange. ( No longer supported . If you're installing Salesforce for the first time, install the Salesforce built integrations for the best experience.) Click Get It Now to install the package to your production or sandbox environment. Select Install for Admins Only . Click Install . Review the list of third-party websites and check the box next to Yes, grant access to these third-party websites . Click Continue . Once installation is complete, click Continue to Setup Assistant .
Note: If your installation takes more than a couple of minutes, Salesforce will send you an email when it's complete.

section.title: Step 3: Grant permissions to use Slack with Salesforce
content: Once the Slack package is installed to Salesforce, it’s important that System Administrators apply the Slack Standard User permission set for all users in your Salesforce org that update record data. Applying this permission set grants users access to Slack actions in your Salesforce org and lets them trigger notifications when records are created or updated. To assign the permission set to Salesforce users, follow the steps below:
Salesforce Lightning
Salesforce Classic

Click the gear icon in the top right and select Setup . Using Quick Find in the top left, search for Permission Sets . Check the box next to Slack Standard User , then click Slack Standard User . Click Manage Assignments . Click Add Assignments . To select users, check the box next to their names, then click Assign . Click Done .

Click Setup in the top right. From the left sidebar, click the arrow next to Manage Users. Below Manage Users, select Permission Sets . Check the box next to Slack Standard User , then click Slack Standard User . Click Manage Assignments . Click Add Assignments . To select users, check the box next to their names, then click Assign . Click Done .

section.title: Step 4: Configure the connection between Salesforce and Slack
content: After the Slack package is installed to Salesforce and users have been assigned the permission set, use the Setup Assistant to configure the connection between your Salesforce org and Slack. You’ll also have the option to configure the settings below:
Custom objects Alerts for standard and custom objects Components on page layouts Custom message destinations
If you don't need to configure a particular setting, click Continue to start the step, then click Finish to move on to the next one.

section.title: Grant Slack access to Salesforce
content: From Salesforce Lightning, open the App Launcher and select the Slack Setup Assistant app. From Salesforce Classic, click the plus button at the top of the page, then find and select Slack Setup from the list. Click Get Started . Click Authorize to grant Slack access to your Salesforce org. Enter your Salesforce credentials, then click Finish . Click Continue to move on to the next step.

section.title: Step 5: Enable custom objects
content: Note: To enable custom objects, make sure you're using Salesforce package version 1.56 or higher.

Enabling a custom object allows you to add Slack actions and the Slack Message Viewer to custom page layouts, and lets members of your workspace subscribe to alerts in Slack. You must enable custom objects before proceeding to the next step to set up custom alerts. This step will only work for custom objects that are not included in the standard set.

Click Add Custom Object . Choose the object you'd like to enable from the drop-down menu. Check the boxes next to the additional fields you'd like to display with the record name in Slack. You can check up to nine. Click Add . Click the Activate link, then select Automatic Activation . If automatic activation fails, you'll need to activate the object manually to make it accessible in your Salesforce org. Click Activate to confirm. Click Finish . Click Continue to move on to the next step.
Once a custom object is activated, you can add the Slack actions and Slack Message Viewer when setting up page layouts ,and create custom alerts.
Note: Once you activate a custom object, it cannot be deactivated.

section.title: Step 6: Set up custom alerts
content: Note: To set up custom alerts, make sure you're using Salesforce package version 1.56 or higher.

A System Administrator can configure custom alerts to expand the default alerts in the package. Once created, members of your Slack workspace or Salesforce org can choose to subscribe to these custom alerts as they would for other object- or record-level alerts.

Click New Alert . Choose a name. Select an object type from the drop-down menu. Choose Object Level or Record Level . Click Next . Select a field, an operator, and a value to set your alert criteria. For example, to set up an alert for quote approvals, you'd choose your custom quote object for the field, an equals operator, and add approved as the value. Add more criteria if you'd like. Note that date fields can't be used in alerts with compound conditions. Click Save . Click Finish . Click Continue to move on to the next step.

section.title: Step 7: Set up page layouts
content: Configure page layouts in Salesforce to send information between Slack and Salesforce.
Note: To remove actions from page layouts, you'll need to use the Object Manager in Salesforce Setup.

section.title: Add Slack actions to layouts
content: There are two types of Salesforce actions available to configure — Send to Slack and Slack Alerts . You can add the Send to Slack action to individual page layouts, or global layouts so it's visible on all pages. To add actions to your page layouts, follow these steps:
Check the box to select your Salesforce environment(s). Review the list of actions and uncheck any you'd like to exclude. Click Add Actions to Layouts . Click Next .

section.title: Add the Slack Message Viewer component to pages
content: To view Slack messages in Salesforce, add the Slack Message Viewer component to your page layouts. Please note that the Message Viewer component is only supported for standard objects in Salesforce Classic.
Uncheck the box next to any page layouts you'd like to exclude from displaying the Message Viewer. Click Add Component to Pages . Click Finish . Click Continue to move on to the next step.
Tip: If you don't see Lightning record pages to choose from, you'll need to create them for your Salesforce org .

section.title: Step 8: Create custom message destinations
content: If you'd like, you can create custom message destinations to send Salesforce information to specific Slack conversations from Process Builder or Flow templates.

section.title: Set up message destinations
content: Click Sign in with Slack to authenticate. Below Configure Message Destinations , click New Message Destination . Enter a message destination name. Select a workspace, then choose a channel or direct message from the drop-down menu. Click Save . Click Finish . Click the file icon to the right of a message destination to copy it so you can add it to the Message Destination ID field in the next step.
Note: If you're on the Slack Enterprise Grid plan, you'll need to sign in to each workspace you'd like to set message destinations for.

section.title: Add message destinations in Process Builder or Flow
content: Once you've set up a message destination, follow the steps below to configure a Process or Lightning Flow to send a Salesforce record to Slack:

For a Process, select Slack: Post Message as the Apex Class. For a Lightning Flow, select Slack: Post Message as the Action. Paste the message destination you copied earlier into the Message Destination ID field. Make sure the Record ID references the ID of the Salesforce record that will be sent to Slack. If you'd like, add message text to send to Slack along with the record. For a Process, add a new row and select Message from the Field drop-down menu. The Type you choose will determine the appropriate Value to enter. For a Flow, toggle Message Input on and enter a value or resource.

section.title: Step 9: Modify Slack settings
content: There are two settings you can change to manage how notifications are sent from Salesforce to Slack:

Trigger record limit The trigger record limit determines when notifications are sent to Slack. If you set your trigger record limit to 10, notifications will only be sent when nine or fewer actions are taken to help prevent a high volume of Slack notifications when you take certain actions in bulk. Async limit The Salesforce app for Slack can consume a maximum of 250,000 asynchronous calls per 24-hour period. The default number of calls set in Salesforce is 240,000 but you can increase this threshold if you’d like. Please note that Slack will only process calls beyond 250,000 when the daily limit resets.
To update these settings, follow the steps below:

From Salesforce Lightning, click the gear icon in the top right and select Setup . From Salesforce Classic, click Setup in the top right. Using Quick Find in the top left corner of the page, search for Custom Settings . Next to Slack Settings, click Manage . Click Edit . Make updates to settings. Click Save .

section.title: Install the Google Drive app to Slack
content: To use the Google Drive app in Slack, one person needs to install the app to your workspace. Once the app is installed, any member can connect their Google account to Slack.

From your desktop, visit the Google Drive page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Click Add Google Drive app . Select Allow . Click Authenticate your Google Drive account . Select the Google account you’d like to connect to Slack. Click Allow .
Tip: Org Owners and Admins in Enterprise organizations can install Google Drive at the org level and add the app to workspaces that need access to it from the admin dashboard.

section.title: Connect your Google Drive account
content: Every member who'd like to use the Google Drive app must connect their Google Drive account to Slack. If you find your account is already connected, your owners or admins have domain-wide authentication enabled, which means your Google account will be connected automatically.

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps in the top left, then search for and select Google Drive to open the app. From the app’s Home tab, click Connect Google Drive and follow the prompts.
Note: If you don't see the Tools tab in your sidebar, look for the Automations tab instead. You may need to click More to find it.

section.title: Create a Google Drive file
content: From any conversation on your desktop, click the slash icon next to the message field. Search for Google Drive , then choose whether you'd like to create a document, presentation, or spreadsheet. Add a title to your file and a message if you’d like. Below Share this document , click the drop-down menu to select a person or channel to share the file with. If you’re not ready to share the file yet, uncheck the box next to Share this document . Click Create .

section.title: Share a Google Drive file
content: From any conversation on your desktop, click the slash icon next to the message field. Search for and select Add from Google Drive . Choose a file, then click Select to share it.
Tip: You’ll see a prompt in Slack to adjust file permissions if some members don’t have access to edit, view, or add comments to the Google Drive file you’ve shared.

section.title: View and reply to comments
content: If someone adds a comment to a file you created or shared, you’ll be notified by the Google Drive app in Slack. Follow these steps to reply to a comment:

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps in the top left, then search for and select Google Drive to open the app. Click the Messages tab at the top of the screen. Hover over a comment and click Start a thread . Type a reply in the message field and send the message to add your comment to the file.

section.title: Manage Google Drive notifications
content: When you connect your Google Drive account to Slack, you’ll automatically receive notifications from the app when someone comments on one of your files, requests access to a file, or shares a file with you. You can enable or disable Google Drive app notifications at any time.

section.title: Enable or disable notifications for all files
content: From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps in the top left, then search for and select Google Drive to open the app. Click the Home tab at the top of the screen. In the Notifications section, click Turn On or Turn Off .

section.title: Manage notifications for specific files
content: If you’d like, you can determine which updates you receive in Slack for a specific Google Drive file:
Open the file in Google Drive. Click the Comments icon in the top-right corner. Choose Notifications , then select which updates you’d like to receive.

section.title: Manage Google Drive file previews
content: When you connect your Google Drive account to Slack, the files will automatically be shared with a rich preview. You can enable or disable Google Drive file previews at any time.

section.title: Enable or disable file previews
content: From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps in the top left, then search for and select Google Drive to open the app. Click the Home tab at the top of the screen. In the File Previews section, click Turn On or Turn Off .

section.title: Disconnect your account
content: If you no longer want to use Google Drive in Slack, you can disconnect your account at any time. This will not uninstall the app from your workspace.

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps in the top left, then search for and select Google Drive to open the app. Click the Home tab at the top of the screen. Click Disconnect Google Drive .
Note: If your organization uses domain-wide authentication , you can disconnect your Google Drive, but you won't be able to disconnect your Google account from Slack.

section.title: What to expect
content: Outlook Calendar for Slack is only available for Office 365. The app isn't supported for on-premise Microsoft Exchange customers. On-premise SharePoint installations or Office 365 plans hosted on a Microsoft national cloud deployment (including Office 365 U.S. Government, Office 365 Germany, and Office 365 operated by 21Vianet in China) aren't supported.

section.title: Add the Outlook Calendar app to Slack
content: To use the Outlook Calendar app in Slack, one person needs to install the app . Once the app is installed, members can connect their calendars to Slack.

section.title: Install the Outlook Calendar app
content: Visit the Outlook Calendar page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Click Allow to grant Outlook Calendar access to Slack. When prompted, click Open Slack to return to your workspace.

section.title: Connect your Outlook account
content: Once the Outlook Calendar app is installed, follow the steps below to connect your account:
Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Connect an account and follow the prompts. Click Open Slack to return to your workspace.

From Home , tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, tap Connect an account and follow the prompts. Tap Done .
Note: If you don't see the Tools tab in your sidebar, look for the Automations tab instead. You may need to click More to find it.

section.title: Connect your calendars
content: You can add as many calendars as you’d like from the account you connected.
Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Connect Calendar . If you have previously connected a calendar, click Settings . Under Accounts , choose a calendar from the drop-down menu. To add additional calendars, reopen the menu and select another calendar. Click Done .

From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, tap Settings and follow the prompts. Under Accounts , choose a calendar from the drop-down menu. To add additional calendars, reopen the menu and select another calendar. Tap Done .
Note: You can only turn on status syncing for your primary calendar.

section.title: Configure personal notification settings
content: Outlook Calendar will send you notifications for all-day events, invitations, updates, and cancellations. You can adjust what you’re notified for, and the timing of your event reminders.
Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Settings . Below your calendar, click Notification Preferences . Set your notification preferences and click Update . Click Done .

From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, tap Settings . Below your calendar, tap Notification Preferences . Set your notification preferences and tap Update .

section.title: Configure channel notification settings
content: If you use a shared calendar or would like an entire channel to be notified about calendar events, you can configure channel notifications.
Desktop
Mobile
Step 1: Add the Outlook Calendar app to a channel

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. Click Outlook Calendar at the top of the app homepage to open the app settings Select Add this app to a channel . From the drop-down menu, search for and select the channel you'd like to configure notifications for. Click Add .
Step 2: Configure channel notifications

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Settings . Below your calendar, click Channel Notifications . Search for and select the channel you’d like to send notifications to, then set your notification preferences and click Update . Click Done .
Step 1: Add the Outlook Calendar app to a channel

Open the channel you'd like to configure Outlook Calendar notifications for. Type /invite @Outlook calendar , then tap the paper plane icon to send the message and allow the app to send notifications to the channel.
Step 2: Configure channel notifications

From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, tap Settings . Below your calendar, tap Channel Notifications . Set your notification preferences and tap Update .

section.title: Create an event
content: Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Create event . Enter a title for your event, then search for and select people to invite. Select which calendar the invite should be sent from. Open the drop-down menu below Select a Calendar . Choose a date and duration. Open the drop-down menu below Available times to select a time when all invitees are available, or select Pick a custom time . If you'd like, add event details in the Description field. To post your event invitation in a channel or direct message (DM), make sure the box next to Share this meeting with is checked. Then, select a conversation from the drop-down menu. Click Create .
From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Create event . Fill out your event details, then tap Create to add the meeting to your calendar.
Anyone you’ve invited will receive a notification in Slack from the Outlook Calendar app. Invitees can respond to your event from that message or from their calendars.
Tip: If the Zoom app has been set as a third-party calling app for your workspace, you can add a Zoom link to your event from the Calling drop-down menu.

section.title: View your schedule and respond to events
content: Desktop
Mobile

From the app's Home tab, click Today , Tomorrow , or Select a date to see all events for a particular date. To view details about an upcoming event, like the location, guest list, and description, click the three dots icon to the right and select View event details . Open the app's Messages tab to respond to events or update responses.

From the Outlook Calendar app's Home tab at the top of the screen, tap Today , Tomorrow , or Select a date to see all events for a particular date. To view details about an upcoming event, like the location, guest list, and description, tap More to the right, then View event details . Open the app's Messages tab to respond to events or update event responses.

Tip: On paid plans , you can receive a daily schedule notification from Outlook Calendar. Open the app's Home tab, then click Settings to enable or disable your daily schedule, or to change the delivery time.

section.title: Automatically update your Slack status
content: Using your calendar, the Outlook Calendar app will automatically set your Slack status to In a meeting , Working remotely , or Out of Office , to help your coworkers know when to expect a reply from you.

Your status will not include the name of the meeting you're attending. You can remove or update your status at any time — the Outlook Calendar app won't override any status you've set yourself. Slack will only sync with the primary calendar for the Outlook account you’ve connected. Only the events you accept, or that mark your availability as Busy , will trigger a status update in Slack. If there are overlapping events on your calendar, Slack will set your status to match the event that’s longer or that starts earlier.
Note: To manage status syncing, open the app's Home tab, then select Settings to turn Status Sync on or off.

images.alt: A Slack status that reads, In a meeting - Outlook Calendar app

section.title: Disconnect a calendar
content: Desktop
Mobile

Click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps in the top left. Search for and select Outlook Calendar to open the app. From the app's Home tab, click Settings . Below the calendar you want to disconnect, click Disconnect Calendar . Click Yes to confirm.

From the Home tab, tap Jump to at the top of the screen and search for Outlook Calendar. Tap Outlook Calendar . From the app's Home tab, tap Settings . Below your calendar, tap Disconnect Calendar . Tap Yes to confirm.
Note: If your organization uses domain-wide authentication , you can disconnect your calendars but, you won't be able to disconnect your Office365 account from Slack.

section.title: Fix calendar syncing issues
content: If events are missing or out of date in the Outlook Calendar app, following the steps below may resolve the problem:
Visit the Outlook Calendar page in the Slack Marketplace. Click the Configuration tab. Below Your Authorization , click Revoke . After the page reloads, click Add to Slack to reconnect your calendar.

section.title: What to expect
content: Office 365 work or school accounts accounts (SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Office 365 Enterprise) and non-Enterprise Microsoft accounts (OneDrive and OneDrive Basic) can use the Microsoft Teams Calls for Slack app. On-premises SharePoint installations or Office 365 plans hosted on a Microsoft national cloud deployment (Office 365 U.S. Government, Office 365 Germany, and Office 365 operated by 21Vianet in China) are not currently supported. Workspace Owners and Admins can choose to set Microsoft Teams Calls as a third-party calling app if they'd like.

section.title: Install the Microsoft Teams Calls app to Slack
content: Any member with permission to add apps can install the Microsoft Teams Calls app to your workspace. Once the app is installed, anyone in your workspace can connect their Office 365 account with Slack to use it.

Visit the Microsoft Teams Calls page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Click Allow to grant Microsoft Teams access to Slack. Sign in to your Microsoft account. When prompted, click Open Slack to go back to your workspace.
Note: If you’re on an Enterprise plan, you’ll need to install the Microsoft Teams Calls app to each workspace in your org where you’d like to use it.

section.title: Connect your Microsoft and Slack accounts
content: If the Microsoft Teams Calls app has already been installed to your workspace, you can connect your account by following the steps below:

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps , then search for and select Microsoft Teams Calls . From the app's Home tab, click Connect . Sign in to your Microsoft account. When prompted, click Open Slack to go back to your workspace.

section.title: Use Microsoft Teams Calls in Slack
Start a meeting
content: From any conversation, click the slash icon in the message field. Type /teams-calls into the search field at the top of the menu. Click Send to message input to add the slash command to the message field. Send the message. All members of the conversation will see a prompt to join the meeting. Click Join . From Microsoft Teams in your browser or the Microsoft Teams desktop app, click Join now to start the meeting.
Tip: Add meeting [subject] after /teams-calls in the message field to start a meeting with a title. For example, you might use /teams-calls meeting [Weekly Sales review] for your team meeting.

section.title: Join a meeting from a channel or DM
content: From a meeting request in Slack, click Join . From your browser, click Open Microsoft Teams . Click Join Now .

section.title: Disconnect your Microsoft and Slack accounts
content: Click the slash icon in the message field. Type /teams-calls logout into the search field at the top of the menu. Click Send to message input . Send the message. Click Yes, sign out .
Note: To uninstall the Microsoft Teams app, follow the steps in Remove apps and custom integrations from your workspace . No one will be able to use the app if you uninstall it.

section.title: What to expect
content: Office 365 accounts (SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Office 365 Enterprise) and non-Enterprise Microsoft accounts (OneDrive and OneDrive Basic) can use the OneDrive and SharePoint Slack app. On-premises SharePoint installations or Office 365 plans hosted on a Microsoft national cloud deployment (Office 365 U.S. Government, Office 365 Germany, and Office 365 operated by 21Vianet in China) are not currently supported. The OneDrive and SharePoint app is compliant under Microsoft's publisher verification program .
Note: When you create and share OneDrive or SharePoint files in Slack, you can search for them in your workspace, but they'll only be stored in OneDrive or SharePoint.

section.title: Connect OneDrive or SharePoint to Slack
content: To use the OneDrive and SharePoint app in Slack, one person in your workspace or Enterprise organization needs to install the app . Then, members can connect their accounts to Slack.
Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

section.title: Install the OneDrive and SharePoint app
content: Visit the OneDrive and SharePoint page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Click Allow to grant OneDrive or SharePoint access to your workspace. When prompted, sign in to your Office 365 account. Click Accept to authenticate with Slack. Click Open Slack to return to your workspace.

section.title: Connect your account
content: Once the OneDrive and SharePoint app is installed to your workspace, follow the steps below to connect your account:

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps , then search for and select OneDrive and SharePoint . From the app’s Home tab, click Connect . Click Allow to grant OneDrive and SharePoint access to your workspace. When prompted, sign in to your Office 365 account. Click Open Slack to return to your workspace.

section.title: Org level
content: From your desktop, click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . From the left sidebar, click Organization , then select Apps to open the admin dashboard. Click Manage Apps in the top right, then click Install an app . Search for and select OneDrive and SharePoint . Click Continue and follow the prompts, then click Allow to grant the app access to your org. From the admin dashboard, click the Installed Apps tab. Find OneDrive and SharePoint, then click the three dots icon to the right of the app. Select Add to more workspaces . Check the box next to any workspaces you’d like to add the app to. To automatically add the app to any new workspaces created in your org, check the box next to Default for future workspaces . Click Next . Check the box next to I’m ready to add this app . Click Add App .

section.title: Workspace level
content: Visit the OneDrive and SharePoint page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Click Allow to grant OneDrive or SharePoint access to your Slack workspace. When prompted, sign in to your Office 365 account. Click Accept to authenticate with Slack. Click Open Slack to return to Slack on your desktop.

Note: In June 2021, we released a new version of the OneDrive and SharePoint app as a Microsoft verified publisher. To update to this version of the app, you can either perform a domain-wide authentication or remove the app and install the latest version from the Slack Marketplace .

section.title: Use OneDrive and SharePoint in Slack
Create files
content: From any conversation, click the slash icon below the message field. Search for OneDrive and SharePoint , then choose whether you'd like to create a document, spreadsheet, or presentation . Enter a title for your file. You can also include a message if you’d like. Below Post file in , open the drop-down menu and select a conversation. Click Create to share your new file.

section.title: Share files
content: From any conversation, click the slash icon below the message field. Search for and select OneDrive and SharePoint . If prompted, sign in to your Office 365 account. Choose which file(s) to share, then click Open .
The first time you share a OneDrive or SharePoint file in Slack, the file will expand to show a preview . Shared files will always include a link back to OneDrive or SharePoint.
Note: It's not currently possible to share folders or OneNote files to Slack.

section.title: Manage file previews
content: When you share a OneDrive or SharePoint file in Slack, you can choose if you'd like a preview to display:

Add a preview A preview will be displayed when you share the file. Don’t add a preview A preview will not be displayed when you share the file, but other file information will be visible. Don’t add a preview or ask me again Previews will never be displayed when you share files, and you won’t see preview prompts.
Tip: To reset your file preview preferences, click Manage Settings from the OneDrive and SharePoint app’s Home tab. Next to Reset preferences , click Reset .

section.title: View recent files
content: From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps , then search for and select OneDrive and SharePoint . From the app’s Home tab, you’ll see any files you’ve accessed recently in Slack, OneDrive, or SharePoint below Recent OneDrive and SharePoint Files .

section.title: Manage access to files
content: If any members don’t have access to view or edit a file you’ve shared with them, you’ll receive a message from the OneDrive and SharePoint app prompting you to adjust access to the file. To change access in the future, you can re-share the file and make adjustments:

Next to a file you’ve shared, open the drop-down menu. Choose who can view the file: Anyone in the conversation , Anyone in your organization , or Anyone with the link . If you’d like, you can also decide who can edit the file: Anyone in your organization or Anyone in the conversation .
Note: Options for managing file access will only be visible for files shared in channels with fewer than 100 people.

images.alt: OneDrive file shared in Slack with prompt to update file visibility

section.title: Disconnect your account
content: If you no longer need to use the OneDrive and SharePoint app, you can disconnect your account. This will not uninstall the app from your workspace.

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Click Apps , then search for and select OneDrive and SharePoint . From the app’s Home tab, click Manage Settings . Next to Disconnect your account , click Disconnect . Click Yes, disconnect to confirm.
Note: If your organization uses domain-wide authentication , you can disconnect your OneDrive and SharePoint accounts, but you won't be able to disconnect your Office365 account from Slack.

section.title: Install the ServiceNow app to Slack
content: To install and configure the ServiceNow app in Slack, you’ll need to be a ServiceNow System Administrator.

section.title: Step 1: Install the ServiceNow app
content: Visit the ServiceNow app page in the Slack Marketplace. Click Add to Slack . Select Allow to grant ServiceNow access to Slack. Click Open Slack to return to your workspace.
Tip: If you’re on an Enterprise plan, you can install the ServiceNow app at the org level and add it to any workspaces that need access to ServiceNow.

section.title: Step 2: Configure ServiceNow OAuth in Slack
content: Note: OAuth must be activated in ServiceNow to use the app in Slack. To activate ServiceNow OAuth, review the setup documentation .

From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps , then search for and select ServiceNow to open the app. From the app’s Home tab, click Prepare OAuth on ServiceNow . You’ll be taken to the ServiceNow website. Create a new OAuth entry in your Application Registry. Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients . Enter Slack in the Name field. Enter https://slack.com/interop-apps/servicenow/snow_oauth_redirect in the Redirect URL field. Enter https://cdn.brandfolder.io/5H442O3W/as/pl546j-7le8zk-ex8w65/Slack_RGB.svg?position=180199 in the Logo URL field. ServiceNow will generate a Client ID and Client Secret . Make sure to keep these handy as you’ll need them to connect ServiceNow to Slack . Click Submit .

section.title: Step 3: Connect ServiceNow to Slack
content: Open the ServiceNow app in Slack. From the app’s Home tab, click Connect ServiceNow to Slack . Enter your ServiceNow Instance URL (ex. acme.service-now.com), Client ID , and Client Secret . Click Submit .

section.title: Step 4: Enable ServiceNow alerts in Slack
content: A Workspace Admin or Owner can enable ServiceNow alerts in Slack. If you aren't able to follow the steps below, find and owner or admin and ask for help. Once alerts are enabled, you and any members of your workspace with the right ServiceNow permissions can set up and configure alerts.

Open the ServiceNow app in Slack. From the app’s Home tab, download the ServiceNow for Slack Notifications Update Set. From Retrieved Update Sets in ServiceNow, upload the Update Set file. Preview and commit the file, then return to the app in Slack. From the Home tab, click Authorize Alerts , then select Authorize alerts . From ServiceNow, assign the x_545827_slack_std.user user permission to grant the ability to add and manage alerts in Slack channels.

section.title: Connect your account
content: If the ServiceNow app has already been installed to your workspace, you can connect your account:
From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps , then search for and select ServiceNow to open the app. From the app’s Home tab, click Connect your account and follow the prompts.

section.title: Create a new incident
content: You can create a new ServiceNow incident from the attachments and shortcuts menu or from a specific message .
Shortcuts menu
From a message

From any conversation, click the slash icon in the message field. Search for Create an Incident with ServiceNow for Slack , then press Enter to select it. Enter details about the incident and click Create .
Hover over a message. Click the three dots icon . Select Create an Incident from the menu. Enter details about the incident and click Create .

section.title: Share ServiceNow records
content: From any conversation, click the slash icon in the message field. Search for Find and share a record from ServiceNow for Slack , then press Enter to select it. Search for a record. Choose a channel and share the record.

section.title: Set up ServiceNow alerts in Slack
content: If a ServiceNow Administrator has enabled alerts, you can set up two kinds of alerts in your workspace:
Record alerts Alerts for an individual record Bulk alerts Alerts for a certain type of record

section.title: Set up an alert
content: From a channel, click the slash icon in the message field. Search for Add/edit channel alerts , then press Enter to select it. Choose a channel from the drop-down menu, then click Next . Select Record alert or Bulk alert . For a record alert, search for and select a record. For bulk alerts, select a record type. Click Next . If you’d like, choose the type of alerts that will post to the channel. Click Save , then click Done .

section.title: Disconnect your account
content: Any workspace member can disconnect their ServiceNow account to stop using the ServiceNow app in Slack. Disconnecting an account will not uninstall the app from your workspace.
From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps , then search for and select ServiceNow to open the app. From the app’s Home tab, click Disconnect accounts and follow the prompts.

section.title: Connect a different ServiceNow instance
content: The ServiceNow administrator who initially installed the app to Slack can change which ServiceNow instance is connected to Slack:
From your desktop, click Tools in the sidebar. Select Apps , then search for and select ServiceNow to open the app. From the app’s Home tab, click Disconnect instance and follow the prompts.
Note: All members of your workspace will need to reconnect their accounts to the ServiceNow app once you’ve connected a new instance.

page: Download a list of members in your workspace

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Workspace Owners / Admins and Org Owners / Admins

section.title: Export a member list
content: From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Manage members from the menu. Click Export full member list at the top of the page.
When your export is ready, you’ll receive a notification with a CSV file you can download to your computer.
Tip: To learn how to export messages and files from your workspace, visit Export your workspace data .
Who can use this feature?
Workspace Owners / Admins and Org Owners / Admins Available on all plans

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: The Org Primary Owner , Workspace Primary Owners , Workspace Owners (Business+) and members with the Roles Admin system role
Available on the Business+ ( select roles ) and Enterprise plans

section.title: Assign members to system roles
content: Business+ plan
Enterprise plans
Workspace Owners can assign individual members to the Workflow Admin , Sales Admin, and Message Activity Manager system roles.

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Manage roles from the menu. Next to the system role you’d like to assign, click the three dots icon and select Assign people . Select members, then click Assign .

section.title: Org level
content: The Org Primary Owner (and any org-level Roles Admins) can assign individual members to system roles. They can also decide if the members will be able to manage the entire org or specific workspaces:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Roles & permissions , then select Roles . Next to the system role you’d like to assign, click the three dots icon and select Assign people . Select members, then click Next . Choose whether these members will manage the org or specific workspaces, then click Save .
Note: Roles Admins cannot assign other members to this role.

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Primary Owners (and any workspace-level Roles Admins) can assign individual members to system roles in workspaces they manage:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Workspace settings . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click Roles & permissions in the left sidebar. Next to the system role you’d like to assign, click the three dots icon and select Assign people . Select members, then click Assign .
Note: Members aren’t notified when system roles have been assigned.

section.title: Modify system roles
content: Business+ plan
Enterprise plans
Workspace Owners can revoke system roles they have assigned:

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Manage roles from the menu. Next to the system role you'd like to modify, click the three dots icon and select View assigned people . Click the three dots icon next to a member’s name and select Revoke role . Click Revoke .

section.title: Org level
content: The Org Primary Owner (and any org-level Roles Admins) can edit and revoke system roles assigned to individuals:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Roles & permissions , then select Roles . Next to the system role you’d like to modify, click the three dots icon and select View assigned people . Click the three dots icon next to a member’s name. Click Edit to make changes, or click Revoke role to revoke a role. Click Save or Revoke to confirm the change.
Note: When you assign a role via IDP group , it can only be revoked by modifying the role for the IDP group.

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Primary Owners (and any workspace-level Roles Admins) can revoke system roles. It’s not possible to modify system roles at the workspace level.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Workspace settings . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click Roles & permissions in the left sidebar. Next to the system role you'd like to modify, click the three dots icon and select View assigned people . Click the three dots icon next to a member’s name and select Revoke role . Click Revoke .

section.title: Manage system roles using IDP groups
content: In an Enterprise org, you can assign and modify system roles using IDP groups .

section.title: Assign roles
content: The Org Primary Owner (and any org-level Roles Admins) can assign IDP groups to system roles. They can also decide if members of the IDP groups will be able to manage the entire org or specific workspaces:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Roles & permissions , then select Roles . Next to the system role you’d like to assign, click the three dots icon and select Assign groups . Select IDP groups to assign, then click Next . Choose whether these members will manage the org or specific workspaces, then click Save .

section.title: Revoke roles
content: The Org Primary Owner (and any org-level Roles Admins) can edit or revoke system roles assigned to IDP groups:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Roles & permissions , then select Roles . Next to the system role you’d like to modify, click the three dots icon and select View assigned groups . Click the three dots icon next to an IDP group. Click Edit to make changes, or click Revoke role to revoke a role. Click Save or Revoke to confirm the change.
Who can use this feature?
The Org Primary Owner , Workspace Primary Owners , Workspace Owners (Business+) and members with the Roles Admin system role Available on the Business+ ( select roles ) and Enterprise plans

page: Invite new members to your workspace

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Workspace Owners , Workspace Admins , and members (by default)

section.title: Send an invitation
content: The ability to send invitations depends on your role in Slack , as well as your workspace settings and plan. An invitation will be active for 30 days after you send it. Owners and admins can resend a pending invitation to reactivate it.

section.title: Free version of Slack
content: On the free version of Slack, owners, admins, and members can invite new members to their workspace.
Desktop
iOS
Android
Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... from the menu. Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite. Click Send , then click Done .
From the DMs tab , tap the plus sign . Tap Invite . Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite, or tap Invite from Contacts to select people saved to your device. Tap Send .
From the DMs tab , tap the plus sign . Tap Invite . Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite, or tap Contacts to invite people saved to your device. Tap Send .
Note: Workspace Owners can approve certain email domains so that anyone with an approved email address can join their workspace.

section.title: Pro, Business+, and Enterprise plans
content: On paid plans, owners, admins, and members can invite new members to their workspace. Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins can also invite guests .
Desktop
iOS
Android

Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... from the menu. Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite. If you're a Workspace Owner or Admin, click the drop-down menu to choose whether you'd like to invite members or guests . If you're inviting members , click Customize your invitation to select additional default channels they'll be added to if they accept their invitations. If you're inviting guests , choose the channel(s) they'll be added to and set a time limit for their accounts if you'd like. Click Send , then click Done .
Note: It's not currently possible to invite guests from Slack's mobile apps.
From the DMs tab , tap the plus sign . Tap Invite . Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite, or tap Invite from Contacts to select people saved to your device. Tap Send .
Note: It's not currently possible to invite guests from Slack's mobile apps.
From the DMs tab , tap the plus sign . Tap Invite . Enter email address for anyone you'd like to invite, or tap Contacts to invite people saved to your device. Tap Send .
Note: On the Enterprise Grid plan, Org Owners can prevent their members from joining external workspaces using an email address on a restricted company domain .

section.title: Share an invitation link
content: On the free, Pro, and Business+ plans, members with permission to send invitations can also share an invite link. Each invite link is active for 30 days, and can be used by up to 400 people. If your invite link expires, find an owner or admin who can manage invite links in Slack.

Keep in mind, anyone who clicks the link will be able to join your workspace. To safeguard the privacy and integrity of your workspace and our platform, be sure to share the link securely, and only with those who should have access to the contents of your workspace.
Desktop
iOS
Android

Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... from the menu. Click Copy invite link . If you’d like, click Edit link settings to choose an expiration date and decide if you’ll receive notifications from Slackbot when someone uses your link.
From the Home tab, swipe right. Tap the three dots icon next to your workspace name. Tap Invite Members . Tap Share a link , then send the link to anyone you'd like to invite.
Note: You won't see the option to create an invite link if single sign-on (SSO) has been enabled for your workspace. If you don't see this option, find an owner or admin to ask for help.

section.title: Request an invitation
content: If members don’t have permission to send invitations, they can request them instead. Members will get a message from Slackbot when an admin has approved or denied their invitation request.
Desktop
iOS
Android

Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... from the menu. Enter the email address for anyone you'd like to invite. If you're on the Pro, Business+, or Enterprise Grid plan, click the drop-down menu to request invitations for members or guests . If you're inviting members , click Customize your invitation to select additional default channels they'll be added to if they accept their invitations. If you're inviting guests , choose the channel(s) they'll be added to and set a time limit for their accounts if you'd like. Click Send Request .

From the Home tab, swipe right. Tap the three dots icon next to your workspace name. Tap Invite Members . Enter the email address of the person you'd like to invite. You'll see the option to enter additional emails once you start typing. Tap Send Request .

From the Home tab, swipe right. Tap the three dots icon next to your workspace name. Tap Invite Members . Enter the email address of the person you'd like to invite. You'll see the option to enter additional emails once you start typing. Tap the check mark . Tap Send Request .

section.title: Invitation limits
content: In certain circumstances, Slack may limit your ability to send invitations. This typically happens if you’ve sent many invites, but few have been accepted. To avoid hitting an invite limit, you can share an invite link instead.
If you hit an invite limit, all of your pending invitations will remain valid. Please note that revoking pending invites will not lift an invitation limit.
Workspace Owners , Workspace Admins , and members (by default) Available on all plans

page: Invite new members to your workspace from your Google Directory

section.title: The basics
content: Any member of a Slack workspace with a G Suite business account can connect their directory to send or request workspace invitations . Your Google Directory contacts will not be stored in Slack, and you can disconnect your directory from Slack at any time. A G Suite administrator at your company may choose to block access to the directory. If you don't see the option to connect your directory in Slack, ask a G Suite admin for help.

section.title: Connect your account
content: To invite members to your workspace using your directory, you'll first need to connect your Google account to Slack.

Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... . Select Add from G Suite . Follow the prompts to grant Slack access to your Google Directory. Click Open Slack to return to your workspace.

section.title: Invite people from your directory
content: Once you've connected your Google account to Slack, follow the steps below to send invitations.

Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... . Select Add from G Suite . Search for specific people or scroll through the list and check the boxes next to anyone you'd like to invite. Click Add , then click Send .
Note: If you don't have permission to send invitations, a request will be sent to your Workspace Owners and Admins to review. Learn more about invitation requests .

section.title: Disconnect or switch your account
content: If you'd like to disconnect your directory from Slack, or switch to another directory account, use the steps below:

section.title: Disconnect your directory
content: Sign in to Google, then visit the Permissions page . Find Slack in the list. Click Remove Access . Click OK .

section.title: Switch your account
content: Click your workspace name in the sidebar. Select Invite people to... . Select Add from G Suite . Click Switch Google account , then follow the prompts to choose another account.
All members (by default) Available on all plans

section.title: What to expect
content: When you mention an invited member or send them a DM, they’ll receive an email notification. If they reply to an email notification, their message will be sent to the appropriate channel, thread, or DM in Slack. Once an invited member joins your workspace, they’ll see any channels they’ve been added to and their DMs so they can continue working in Slack. Invited members can't see the contents of messages or reply by email if their email address is on a social domain (for example, Gmail), their email address does not match the domain of the sender, or if your workspace or Enterprise organization is HIPAA-enabled . If an invited member unsubscribes from email notifications , this won't affect their invitation. They can still join your workspace in the future.
Tip: Workspace Owners and Admins can choose to hide message content in emails sent to certain domains from Workspace Settings .

section.title: Accounts and billing
content: While an invited member can receive email notifications and reply to messages in Slack via email, they do not yet have an active Slack account. An invited member's account becomes active when they accept their invitation and sign in to your Slack workspace for the first time.
If you're on a paid plan, you will not be billed for invited members until they become active in Slack. To learn more about how you're billed, read our Fair Billing Policy .

section.title: Manage invitations
content: Workspace Owners and Admins can manage pending invitations from the Manage members page . Org Owners and Admins can manage invitations from the admin dashboard .

When you add people to Slack using SCIM provisioning , pre-provisioned invited members will be visible in Slack as soon as they're added via your identity provider (IDP). Until they sign in for the first time, they'll receive emails whenever someone in Slack notifies them. They can also reply to Slack messages by email. Users provisioned with just-in-time provisioning will not be visible in Slack until they log in.

If you revoke an invited member's invitation, their Slack account will be deactivated and they'll stop receiving email notifications. Should you re-invite them to Slack in the future, they'll be treated as a new invited member until they join your workspace.

section.title: Notify invited members
content: On paid plans, owners and admins can notify invited members about any messages in channels where invited members have been added:
Hover over the message you’d like to share. Click the three dots icon and select More message shortcuts from the menu. Select Notify pending members . Click Send Email .
Pending members will receive an email notification with a preview of the message. They can then choose to open the message in Slack or reply by email.

page: Manage pending invitations and invite links for your workspace

section.title: Manage pending invitations
content: You can resend or extend invitations to give invited members more time to accept. If you change your mind, you can also delete an invitation to prevent an invited member from accepting it.

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click People . Click Invitations . Select the Pending tab at the top of the page. Next to the invitation you’d like to manage, click Extend Invitation , Resend Invitation , or Delete Invitation .

section.title: Manage invitation links
content: You can view all invite links for your workspace, including who set them up and when they were created. You can also deactivate any you no longer want to be in use, or renew expired links if you'd like to keep using them.

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click People . Click Invitations . Select the Invite links tab at the top of the page to view the active links for your workspace. If you’d like, click Deactivate next to any link you’d like to disable.
Who can use this feature?
Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins Available on all plans

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Org Owners / Admins and Workspace Owners / Admins

section.title: Who can manage roles
content: Only people in administrative roles can manage roles for other members and guests. Here’s an overview of the actions each administrative role can take:
Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

section.title: Workspace-level permissions
content: Tip: The current Primary Owner of a workspace or org can transfer ownership to another member, but only one person can have that role a time.

section.title: Manage owner and admin roles
content: Review your role's permissions , then use the steps below to promote or demote owners and admins.
Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click People . Click the three dots icon next to the member whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . To promote someone, select Workspace Owner or Workspace Admin . To demote someone, click Workspace Admin or Regular Member . Click Save.

section.title: Org level

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select Members . Search for a member, then click their name to view their profile. Click Manage in the top right. To promote someone, choose Make Org Owner or Make Org Admin . To demote someone, choose Remove from Org Admins .

section.title: Workspace level
content: Org Owners and Admins can manage workspace-level administrative roles from the admin dashboard.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . Click Workspaces , then select All workspaces and choose a workspace. Click People , then click Members & guests . Click the three dots icon next to the member whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . To promote someone, select Workspace Owner or Workspace Admin . To demote someone, select Workspace Admin or Regular Member .
Workspace Owners and Admins can manage administrative roles for their workspace(s).

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Manage members . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click the three dots icon next to the member whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . To promote someone, select Workspace Owner or Workspace Admin . To demote someone, click Workspace Admin or Full Member . Click Save.
Tip: Org Owners and Workspace Owners can assign members to system roles to help with specific administrative tasks.
Note: If you don't see Admin in your sidebar, click your workspace name to access workspace settings instead.

section.title: Manage guest roles
content: On the Pro, Business+, and Enterprise plans, you can invite guests to your workspace(s) . Use the steps below to manage guest roles.

section.title: Change a guest's role
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click People . Click the three dots icon next to the guest whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . Select Regular Member , Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest and click Save or Next . If you chose Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest , enter the channel(s) the guest will have access to and set a time limit if you’d like. Then, click Make Multi-Channel Guest or Make Single-Channel Guest .
Note: Members can request to add Single-Channel Guests to additional channels. Workspace Owners and Admins will receive a message to approve or deny these upgrade requests.

section.title: Org level
content: If a guest belongs to multiple workspaces, Org Owners and Admins can change them to a regular member.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select Members . Search for a guest, then click their name to view their profile. Click Manage in the top right and select Make Org Member .
Note: A user cannot be a guest in some workspaces but a member in others.

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Owners and Admins can change a guest to a regular member if the guest only belongs to one workspace.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Manage members . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click the three dots icon next to the guest whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . Select Regular Member , Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest and click Save or Next . If you selected Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest , enter the channel(s) the guest will have access to and set a time limit if you’d like. Then, click Make Multi-Channel Guest or Make Single-Channel Guest .
Note: To promote guests to Workspace Owners or Admins, you'll need to make them a regular member first, then promote them .

section.title: Change a regular member to a guest
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click People . Click the three dots icon next to the member whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . Select Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest and click Next . Enter the channel(s) the guest will have access to and set a time limit if you'd like. Click Make Multi-Channel Guest or Make Single-Channel Guest .

section.title: Org level
content: If a regular member belongs to multiple workspaces, Org Owners and Admins can change them to a guest by deactivating their account, then reactivating them as a guest.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select Members . Click the three dots icon next to the member you'd like to change and select Deactivate this account . To reactivate the member as a guest, click View Deactivated Members . Click the three dots icon next to the member you'd like to change and select Reactivate as Multi-Channel Guest or Reactivate as Single-Channel Guest .
Once you've reactivated the guest, add them to a workspace to choose their channel membership.

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Owners and Admins can change a regular member to a guest if the member only belongs to one workspace.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Manage members . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click the three dots icon next to the member whose role you'd like to change and select Change account type . Select Multi-Channel Guest or Single-Channel Guest and click Next . Enter the channel(s) the guest will have access to and set a time limit if you'd like. Click Make Multi-Channel Guest or Make Single-Channel Guest .
Note: To convert Workspace Owners and Admins to guests, you’ll need to change them to a regular member first.

page: Create a link to a member's profile

section.title: Create a link to a DM or profile
content: Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans
Create the link by combining your workspace URL with members’ user IDs. Here’s how:

The first part of the link is the w orkspace URL . For example, https://acmeco.slack.com . The second part of the link is the u ser ID . Multiple members' User IDs can be found using the users.list API method . Or, an individual's User ID can be found by clicking the More button in a member's profile, then choosing Copy member ID . Append the user ID to the end of the workspace URL. Here’s an example: https://acmeco.slack.com/team/U1H63D8SZ. That’s it! Include this link to a member’s profile anywhere you’d like.
Create the link by combining your org URL with members’ org-level user IDs. Here’s how:

The first part of the link is the o rg URL . Let’s say it’s https://acmeorg.enterprise.slack.com . The second part of the link is the member's org-level u ser ID . Multiple members' user IDs can be found using the SCIM GET /Users API method . Or, a n individual's user ID can be found by clicking the More button in a member's profile, then choosing Copy member ID . Append the user ID to the end of the org URL. Like so: https://acmeorg.enterprise.slack.com/user/@W1H63D8SZ. That’s it! Include this link to a member’s profile anywhere you’d like.
All members Available on all plans

section.title: Org level
content: Org Owners and Org Admins can make name changes for members of their organization:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select Members . Find the member you'd like to update, and click their full name. Click Edit Profile . Enter a new full name, display name, or username and click Save Changes .

section.title: Workspace level
content: Workspace Owners and Workspace Admins can make name changes for members of their individual workspace(s):

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Manage members . If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu. Click the three dots icon to the right of the member's name you'd like to edit. Click Edit profile. Enter a new full name or display name and click Save .

Note: You can't edit profiles that have the same or a higher role than you. For example, if you're a Workspace Owner, you can't change another Workspace Owner's profile or the Workspace Primary Owner's profile.

section.title: Set guest permissions for name editing
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans
Workspace Owners can choose if guests can edit their full name and display name in their profile.

Click Edit permission . Choose whether Multi-channel Guests or Single-channel Guests can edit their name, then click Save .
Org Owners and Org Admins can choose if guests can edit their full name and display name in their profile.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select Manage permissions . Select Account Types . Click the three dots icon next to Edit name , then select Edit permission . Choose whether Multi-channel Guests or Single-channel Guests can edit their name, then click Save .
Note: Org Owners and Org Admins on Enterprise plans can also prevent members from editing certain profile fields .
Tip: Owners and admins that manage profiles using SCIM can update members' names from within their identity provider (IDP). Changes will be refreshed the next time the members sign in to Slack.
