section.title: Claim and verify domains
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

When you claim email domains your members will only be able to accept Slack Connect invitations from domains you have claimed. This ensures that members can only accept Slack Connect invitations from the workspaces you manage.

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click Security . Click Email domains . Click Add Domain . In the domain field, enter the domain (or wildcard domain) you’d like to verify, then click Next . You'll need access to a Domain Name System (DNS) to confirm the domain belongs to your organization. Follow instructions provided by your domain hosting service to create a DNS TXT record (for Host, use @ if the domain is not a wildcard and _slack-challenge if it is). It may take up to 72 hours for changes to take effect. After confirming your TXT record is added to your DNS, return to Email Domains on your Slack admin dashboard. Next to a domain, select Verify domain in the status column, then click Next . If you'd like, set your org as the primary organization for Slack Connect.
When you verify and restrict email domains, you can choose to limit your members’ ability to join new workspaces in the following ways:

Accepting Slack Connect invites Your members will only be able to accept Slack Connect invitations from domains you have claimed. This ensures that members can only accept Slack Connect invitations from the workspaces you manage. Joining external workspaces Members of other workspaces won’t be able to send invitations to email addresses on domains that your organization has claimed. If you claim a domain after an invitation has been sent, your members won’t be able to accept it.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . From the left sidebar, click Security , then Email Domains . Click Add Domains . In the domain field, enter the domain (or wildcard domain) you’d like to verify. Choose to apply domain claiming restrictions on joining external workspaces or accepting Slack Connect invitations, then click Next . You'll need access to a Domain Name System (DNS) to confirm the domain belongs to your organization. Follow instructions provided by your domain hosting service to create a DNS TXT record (for Host, use @ if the domain is not a wildcard and _slack-challenge if it is). It may take up to 72 hours for changes to take effect. After confirming your TXT record is added to your DNS, return to Email Domains on your Slack admin dashboard. Next to a domain, select Verify domain in the status column, then click Next . If you'd like, set your org as the primary organization for Slack Connect.
Tip: You can also claim domains for your Enterprise org to prevent people from creating unsanctioned workspaces and make your org’s workspaces easier to find.

section.title: I'm the Primary Owner
content: If you’re the Primary Owner of a workspace or Enterprise org, you can transfer ownership to another member.

section.title: What to expect
content: You'll need to enter your password to confirm the transfer. The transfer will happen immediately. Your role will change from Primary Owner to Owner. Need to deactivate your account ? You'll need to transfer primary ownership first.

section.title: Transfer ownership
content: Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

Visit the transfer ownership page . Search for and select the member you'd like to be the new Workspace Primary Owner. Enter your password to confirm the transfer. Click the Transfer Workspace Ownership button to finish.
There are two types of primary ownership within an Enterprise org — a single Org Primary Owner, and multiple Workspace Primary Owners.

section.title: Transfer ownership of a workspace
content: In an Enterprise org, Workspace Primary Owners can transfer ownership of their workspace to another member.

Visit the transfer ownership page . Search for and select the member you'd like to be the new Workspace Primary Owner. Enter your password to confirm the transfer. Click the Transfer Workspace Ownership button to finish.

section.title: Transfer ownership of an org
content: The Primary Org Owner can choose to transfer primary ownership to another member. If you're the Org Primary Owner, here's how to contact us:
Use this form to send us a note . Include the new Org Primary Owner's email address. Our team will get in touch to help you complete the transfer.
Tip: Consider working with your new Primary Owner to ensure details like billing information remain accurate.

section.title: I'm not the Primary Owner
content: Free, Pro, and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

section.title: Step 1: Contact the Primary Owner
content: Only a Primary Owner can transfer ownership. Try reaching out to the Primary Owner first to request that they transfer their role directly to someone else. If you're not sure who the Primary Owner is, visit the About This Workspace page to confirm.

If the Primary Owner is no longer available (for example, if they’ve left your organization or can’t be reached), Slack may be able to help transfer the Primary Owner role. Review the steps below to see if your workspace qualifies and what information you’ll need to include when you contact us.
Note: Slack may be able to help transfer the Primary Owner role for workspaces owned by a company, institution, or other legal entity, but we can’t guarantee that every situation will qualify.

section.title: Step 2: Check if your workspace qualifies
content: Slack can only consider requests to transfer the Primary Owner role if both the following criteria are met:

The workspace was created on behalf of a legal entity, such as a company, organization, or educational institution The request is submitted or authorized by a senior staff member who can represent that entity, such as a director-level employee or someone in an equivalent leadership position.
If these requirements aren’t met, Slack may not be able to transfer the Primary Owner role.

If the workspace was created by the Primary Owner on their own behalf (for example, to support a personal project, club, or community group) and not on behalf of a company or other legal entity, Slack cannot assist with a request to transfer the Primary Owner role.

section.title: Step 3: Gather what you’ll need
content: Before contacting Slack for assistance, make sure you have the following information ready.

The workspace URL (for example, yourworkspace.slack.com) Primary Owner details : Who currently holds the role, their email address, and how that account is connected to your organization. The proposed new Primary Owner: Include the name and email address of the person you’d like to transfer the Primary Owner role to. Make sure they’re already a member of your workspace, and their account uses an email address on your company’s domain — we can’t transfer ownership to personal email addresses.

section.title: Step 4: Submit your request
content: After you’ve tried internal options and confirmed your workspace qualifies, reach out to Slack Support . We’ll review the details, and follow up with next steps if we need more information from you.
Please keep in mind that transfers of the Primary Owner role go through a careful review process, may take time, and aren’t guaranteed to be approved.
If your Org Primary Owner has left the organization or can’t be reached, Slack can help transfer the org primary owner role to another member. Here’s how to contact us:
Use this form to send us a note . Include the new Org Primary Owner's email address. Our team will get in touch to help you complete the transfer.
Tip: You can always create your own workspace if needed — this would make you the Primary Owner of the new workspace.
Only the Primary Owner can transfer ownership of a workspace or org Available on all plans

section.title: TOS overview

section.title: What you can do
content: Sync profile fields with your identity provider (IDP) to automatically populate them. Add and manage custom profile fields to fit your needs. Create an org chart for your members to easily get insight into your organization’s reporting hierarchy.

section.title: Populate profile fields
content: With Slack Atlas, you can choose from three methods to update your profile fields:

SCIM API Automatically populate profile fields configured in your IDP or via a custom SCIM connector . Web API Use the web API to set or retrieve profile fields. Member edit Members can update profile fields manually.
Note: When you map a profile field using SCIM or Web API, the field can't be manually edited by members.

section.title: Custom profile fields and modules
content: Slack Atlas profiles are made up of groups of profile fields called modules. You can choose from a variety of standard data types (like short text or date) when you create a profile field. In addition to the standard data types in Slack profiles, Slack Atlas provides two more options:

Long text provides up to 5,000 characters of text entry for long form fields, like a detailed "About me" section. Smart tags support profile fields with multiple values, like language abilities or training certifications.

View-only profiles are created by appending [[profile-only]] to the value in the userType field using the SCIM API .

page: Migrate workspaces to an Enterprise organization

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?

section.title: Before migration
content: Workspaces on the Free, Pro, and Business+ plans can be migrated into your Enterprise org. As you prepare to migrate a workspace, there are a few things to keep in mind:

Account provisioning If the migrating workspace uses SAML to manage identity, turn off account provisioning in your identity provider (IDP) to prevent accounts from being de-provisioned when you disable the connector. You can also minimize migration downtime and prevent duplicate accounts by assigning access to new members after the migration is complete. Custom profile fields Any custom profile fields in the migrating workspace will not be carried over. These fields will need to be set up again after the migration is complete. Guest access If you intend to allow guests to sign in with their email address and password, ensure your org settings allow them to bypass SSO . Workspace settings Your org's settings and policies will override individual workspace settings. Depending on permissions, Workspace Owners and Admins may be able to make adjustments to their workspace settings. Audit logs If your workspace uses audit logs , you'll need to export your logs to access them once the migration is complete.

section.title: Initiate a migration
content: You can start a migration from the admin dashboard. You’ll need the ID and URL of the workspace that you’re migrating.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Workspaces , then select Migrations . Enter the workspace ID and URL, then click Send Migration Request .
The Workspace Primary Owner will receive a notification from Slackbot where they can approve or deny the migration request.

section.title: Complete the migration checklist
content: Once your migration has been approved by the Workspace Primary Owner, we'll provide you with a checklist to ensure you complete all necessary tasks.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Workspaces , then select Migrations . Select a workspace to open the migration checklist.

Set up SSO (single sign-on) To proceed with your migration, set up SSO for your org (if you haven’t already). Make sure your new members can access Slack after the migration by matching the email domain in your SSO provider to the email domain for new users migrating into your org. Confirm matching user accounts If the workspace you’re migrating contains accounts with the exact same email address and account type as accounts on your org, you can choose to merge them. Resolve conflicting user accounts Conflicting user accounts share some of the same profile fields, but not enough to be exact matches. If the workspace contains partial account matches, review them individually from the Migrating users tab and choose an action. Review conflicting settings If your org's settings differ from the migrating workspace, you can review them from the Conflicting settings tab. Adjust settings if you'd like then click Confirm Settings to finish. Schedule your migration When you're ready, click Schedule Migration to complete the checklist and schedule your migration. Follow the prompts to select a date and time for your migration.

section.title: During migration
content: Below is an overview of how Org Owners can view and manage migrations, plus what to expect once the migration is underway.
Note: Migrations of larger workspaces may take a few hours to complete. We recommend giving members advance notice to avoid disruption.

section.title: What to expect during a migration
content: The migrating workspace will be unavailable to members for a portion of the migration. Members can use their workspace while direct messages (DMs) migrate in the background. Typically, the Enterprise org will be accessible to existing members throughout the migration. Members will receive a message shortly before the migration begins to let them know their workspace will be temporarily unavailable. Slack Connect conversations between the migrating workspace and org won’t be accessible to either organization. After the migration, Slack Connect channels will become org-wide multi-workspace channels and they’ll use the privacy setting of the channel in the org. Members from the migrating workspace will receive an email and Slackbot message when the migration is complete.

section.title: View and manage migrations
content: Org Owners can cancel upcoming migrations and view the status of any that are in progress:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Workspaces , then click Migrations . Click the three dots icon next to a migration, then click Cancel migration .

section.title: After migration
content: Once migration is complete, here's what to expect:

Message history, files, apps, and emoji Members will have access to channel and direct message (DM) history, files, custom emoji, and apps (including custom integrations and webhooks). DMs across workspaces will be merged together. Profiles During the migration process, members' profile details are merged based on the options you choose in the migration checklist . If more than one workspace was moved, profile details from the first workspace will be applied by default. Members can always update their profile after migrating if needed. Salesforce features Features that rely on a connection to Salesforce (such as Salesforce channels , Agentforce , or Sales Home ) will be migrated to the Enterprise organization. Workspace access By default, any org member can request to join the migrated workspace. Org Owners can adjust how members find and join the workspace by changing the access preference . Member access The migrated workspace’s URL will redirect to your org's sign-in page. New members and guests will sign in using the method set in your SSO settings . Workspace roles The Workspace Primary Owner role for any migrated workspaces will be re-assigned to the Org Primary Owner. The former Workspace Primary Owner will become a Workspace Owner.
Have migration questions? Reach out to our Support team for help.
Who can use this feature?
Org Owners Available on the Enterprise Grid and Enterprise+ plans

page: A guide to Slack's Discovery APIs

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: The Primary Org Owner and Org Owners

section.title: How it works
content: Many customers enlist a third-party eDiscovery or Data Loss Prevention (DLP) partner to house all of their cloud solution software. Our Discovery API connects Slack Enterprise organizations to a customer’s partner of choice.

section.title: Discovery API
content: Our Discovery API lets Org Owners on Enterprise plans use approved third-party apps to export or act on messages and files from Slack. The Primary Org Owner or an Org Owner can request to enable the Discovery API. Once enabled, it will be accessible to all Org Owners.
There are two types of third-party partner apps, depending on your needs:

eDiscovery eDiscovery apps pull messages and files from Slack, and store the information in third-party data warehouses. From the data warehouses, messages and files can be searched, archived, or retrieved. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) DLP apps ensure confidential information (like credit card and social security numbers) isn’t shared outside of Slack by scanning for content within messages and files that break predefined policies.

section.title: Step 1: Evaluate your needs
content: Whether you decide to use an eDiscovery or DLP tool will depend on the needs of your organization. Here are some scenarios to help you select the right solution to use in partnership with the Discovery API:
eDiscovery
DLP

Customers may use eDiscovery for one-off civil or criminal legal cases, or to replicate and keep a record of all message and file data for compliance purposes. Here's an overview of how eDiscovery apps work:
They typically have read-only access to Slack message and file data Data can't be quarantined, removed, or tagged within Slack Data is captured and archived within a data warehouse
Note: Archiving does not disrupt or impact how members interact with a workspace.
By detecting and removing potential threats, DLP third-party tools allow you to secure your data from within. DLP apps can do the following:

Have read and write access in Slack Ensure confidential information (like social security numbers) isn't shared within your Slack workspaces Allow authorized personnel to manage workspace activity and enforce predefined policies on messages and files shared in Slack Allow quarantined messages and files to be reviewed or removed

section.title: Step 2: Choose a partner
content: Many enterprises want a one-stop shop to house all of their cloud solutions. Slack works with a number of third-party eDiscovery and DLP partners. Here's a list of our current third-party partners to choose from:
eDiscovery
DLP

MirrorWeb Nuix Onna OpenText Axcelerate Pagefreezer Proofpoint Red Deer Relativity Smarsh SteelEye Theta Lake Transcend ZL Technologies 17a-4 DataParser
Astrix Security Avanan Aware BigID Bitglass CloudLock DoControl Entro Security FireEye Fortra (formerly Digital Guardian) Gamma Lookout Metomic
McAfee VISION Cloud (Skyhigh for Slack) Netskope Nightfall (formerly Watchtower) Obsidian Security Palo Alto Networks Polymer Proofpoint Reco.ai Symantec Theta Lake Zscaler

section.title: Step 3: Data access and format
content: The Discovery API allows Org Owners to export messages and files (PDFs, JPGs, etc.) from any workspace within an Enterprise Grid organization. An export will include data starting from the date a workspace was created until present time.
Data exported via the Discovery API comes in JSON format. If a different format is required, the Discovery API can be connected to a third-party eDiscovery or DLP app.

content: The first time a new member signs in to the organization, they'll be asked to review our terms of service. Include an additional custom Terms of Service for your company, if you'd like. 📜✨
By clicking I Agree , they'll be able to proceed to the next step.

content: Next, we help your members find the right workspace(s) to join so they can get up and running as quickly as possible.
If a member was already invited or provisioned to a specific workspace, they'll be taken to that workspace.
If they're not assigned a specific workspace, they'll have a couple of options:

page: Manage a workspace in an Enterprise organization

section.title: Step 1: Create a workspace in your org
content: You can move an existing Slack workspace to your org, or create a new one.
🚛  Move a workspace to an organization
Org Owners can work with Slack to move selected workspaces into an Enterprise org. Once moved, a workspace will retain all member accounts, messages, files — even emoji reactions!
A workspace's Primary Owner must approve the move to an org. They'll receive an email and Slackbot message requesting approval, and can click Respond to Invitation to begin the process.
💡 Read our Guide to moving workspaces to an organization .
🌱  Create a new workspace
You can request that an Org Owner or Admin create a new workspace on your organization . If approved, you'll get an email and Slackbot message letting you know that you’re the Workspace Owner.
💡 Learn how to request a new workspace in your organization .

section.title: Step 2: Workspace settings and permissions
content: Manage your workspace's settings and permissions from the desktop app:

From your desktop, click your organization name in the top left. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Workspace settings . (If you manage more than one workspace, choose one from the drop-down menu.)
Some of your workspace policies are controlled by Org Owners and Org Admins. If you see a lock icon , that means the preference is locked by an Org Admin.
Tip: Learn more about the roles available in Slack and the permissions each role has in an Enterprise org.
🔐  Workspace access
You can decide how members of your org access and join your workspace:

Open: Visible to all members and open to join By Request: Visible to all, but members must ask permission to join Invite Only: Visible to all, but members must be invited to join Hidden: Unlisted and new members must be invited to join
💡 Learn how to manage workspace access .

section.title: Step 3: Add members to your workspace
content: Now that you’ve created a workspace, it’s time to add members! Depending on your needs, there are a couple ways to do this:
Add members by inviting them to your workspace . Work with an Org Owner to add groups of people (like a department) from your company’s identity provider (IDP) .
💡 Learn how to add members to a workspace in an organization .

section.title: 🔗Create multi-workspace channels
content: Multi-workspace channels let people in different workspaces seamlessly connect. You decide who has access to these channels: a specific set of workspaces or all workspaces in the org. You can make them private too!
💡Learn how to add channels to other workspaces .
Note: If multi-workspace channel creation is disabled for Workspace Admins and members, get in touch with an Org Owner or Org Admin for help.
📺  Move channels between workspaces

As your org grows and workspaces expand, it's only natural that the right place for a discussion may change. Help keep everyone focused and productive by moving channels from a less relevant workspace to a more appropriate one.
You'll need to be a Workspace Owner or Admin on both the channel’s original and destination workspaces to make the move.
💡 Learn how to move channels between workspaces .
Step 5: Apps and tools
Slack lets you connect all of the tools and services you use for work in one place, eliminating the need to switch between apps.
👩‍💻  Add apps to your workspace
You can find apps for services you already use in the Slack Marketplace — including tools for payments & accounting, project management, HR, and beyond.
💡 Visit Add an app to your workspace for detailed instructions.
Note: Apps and bots work best when installed to all of the workspaces that share channels.
🤖  Build internal integrations

In addition to the Slack Marketplace, you can build custom integrations that are tailored to your workspace's needs. Though it requires some technical skill, creating your own integrations can have huge benefits:
Keep existing internal tools your company is familiar with. Pull updates from other services into Slack to centralize info. Consolidate data from various analytic dashboards into Slack.
💡 Learn how to customize Slack with internal integrations .

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Org Owners and Org A dmins

section.title: What to expect
content: Connect workspaces to automatically add or remove members of an IDP group to workspaces within your org. You can make membership for certain workspaces required to ensure that all members of an IDP group remain members of a workspace. Connect channels to automatically add members of an IDP group to channels within your org. Channels can be public or private and shared with external organizations, but they must be accessible from a required workspace in order to be connected to an IDP group.
Note: You must have permission to manage channels to connect IDP groups to channels.

section.title: Connect workspaces
content: Org Owners and Org Admins can automatically add or remove members from workspaces using IDP groups. Connecting a workspace to an IDP group will not impact members who are already a part of the workspace. Removing members from an IDP group will only remove them from required workspaces .
Connect
Disconnect

section.title: Connect a workspace
content: From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select [IDP name] Groups . Search for and select an IDP group. Click Connect Workspaces and check the box next to every workspace you’d like to connect. You can search for workspaces to filter your results. Click Next . To make workspace membership required, click the toggle next to Make all workspaces required or next to individual workspaces. Click Connect Workspaces .
Note: Members can’t deactivate their accounts when workspace membership is required.

section.title: Make workspace membership required
content: Org Owners and Org Admins can make workspace membership mandatory for all members of an IDP group at any time.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select [IDP name] Groups . Search for and select an IDP group. Click the Workspaces tab. Click the three dots icon next to the workspace you’d like to edit. Click Make membership required .

section.title: Disconnect a workspace
content: Warning: Disconnecting an IDP group from a workspace will automatically remove all members in that group from that workspace.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click People in the left sidebar, then select [IDP name] Groups . Search for and select an IDP group. Click the Workspaces tab. Click the three dots icon next to the workspace you’d like to disconnect. Click Disconnect workspace .

section.title: Connect channels
content: Note: Channels can be public or private and shared with external organizations , but they must be org-wide multi-workspace channels or accessible from a required workspace in order to be connected to an IDP group.

Org Owners and Org Admins can connect IDP groups to channels to automatically add members to channels. These will be default channels for all members of the IDP group, but they can leave these channels at any time, if they’d like.
Connect
Disconnect

You can search for channels by name or workspace to filter your results. Click Connect .

section.title: Disconnect a channel

Click People in the left sidebar, then select [IDP name] Groups . Search for and select an IDP group. Click the Channels tab. Click the three dots icon next to the channel you’d like to disconnect. Click Disconnect channel .

section.title: Why claim domains?
content: Make your org's connected workspaces easier to find. Prevent people from creating unsanctioned workspaces outside of your org. Allow people with email addresses in specific domains to join your org.

section.title: What to expect with claimed domains

Existing members of your org will see a message (with a contact link included) directing them to contact an Org Admin for help. People that have yet to join your org will have the option to use single sign-on to create an account, plus use the included contact link to reach out to an Org Admin for help.

Note : Once a domain is claimed, it will be removed from the signup mode for any workspace using the domain that does not belong to your Enterprise org. Members will no longer see these workspaces listed when signing into Slack .

By default, the included contact link will direct to the Org Primary Owner's email address. Org Owners can customize this link by selecting which contact email address is included using the steps below.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . From the left sidebar, select Settings , then click Organization settings . Next to Maximum expiration for guests , click Edit . Select an option and click Save .

page: Use Slack Connect with free teams

section.title: Manage connections with free teams
content: Org Owners and Org Admins can manage a setting to determine whether free teams can be invited to Slack Connect channels. If you change this setting, only future invitations sent from your organization will be affected.

From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Select Tools & settings from the menu, then click Organization settings . section.title: What to expect for free teams
content: Here are some more details on what free teams can expect when working with your company in Slack Connect channels:

Whether messages and files (including canvases and lists) remain visible depends on the free workspace’s retention settings . With a one-year retention policy, messages and files older than one year will be deleted, except for those in Slack Connect channels. With a 90-day retention policy, messages and files will be deleted from all channels after 90 days. Channel members can start and join huddles , record audio and video clips , add and use apps , and use workflows in the channel. People from free teams can join Slack Connect channels they’re invited to, but cannot send invitations to additional organizations.

page: Set up and manage Agentforce in Slack

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?
roles: Workspace Owners / Admins (Free, Pro, and Business+ plans) Org Owners / Admins (Enterprise plans)
Available on all Slack plans with a Salesforce Agentforce license

section.title: How it works
content: Build and customize agents in Salesforce, then add them to Slack to make them available to your members. Once they’ve been added to Slack, members can find and message agents they have access to the Agents tab or message them in channels .
Learn more about Agentforce: Visit our launch guide or contact your Slack Account Executive .

section.title: Build an agent in Salesforce
content: Use the guidance below to get started with creating an agent using Agentforce Builder in Salesforce:

Create an agent using pre-made templates for Slack. Customize your agent with topics and actions to define its scope and expertise. Add the General Slack Actions topic to your agent to choose from a set of Slack actions like creating a canvas (not available on the free version of Slack ), performing a search , and more.
Note: You can only build agents for Slack using the Agentforce Employee Agent type .

section.title: Agent templates for Slack
content: Agent templates allow you to quickly create an agent to handle common tasks. When creating an agent from a template , search for Slack to view the available templates. There are three agent templates available for Slack:

Customer Insights Agent Uses Salesforce data to summarize customer information, find subject matter experts in Slack, and generate customer briefs. Employee Help Agent Resolves internal issues by answering frequently asked questions using internal resources and conversations in Slack. Onboarding Agent Helps onboard new team members by creating onboarding canvases and answering frequently asked questions from custom knowledge bases.

section.title: Connect Salesforce and Slack
content: To set up Agentforce in Slack, connect your Salesforce organization to Slack. Coordinate with an Admin in Salesforce to complete any setup steps in Salesforce.

section.title: Step 1: Connect a Salesforce org to Slack
content: Follow the steps in our Connect Salesforce and Slack guide. Once your Salesforce org is connected, you’ll need to manually map users if they haven’t already been granted access to Salesforce in Slack.

section.title: Step 2: Install the Slack connected app for the legacy agent builder
content: If you’re using the legacy agent builder , install the Slack connected app. Proceed to the next step if you’re using Salesforce’s new Agentforce Builder .
From Salesforce, select Setup . In the Quick Find box, search for and select Connected Apps OAuth Usage . Scroll down to Slack , then select Install on the right. Click Install to finish.
Note: People in Slack that don’t have a Salesforce account will need a provisional Salesforce license to access Agentforce in Slack. Reach out to your Salesforce Account Executive to learn more.

section.title: Step 3: Map accounts
content: Connect your members’ Salesforce and Slack accounts. When you manually map members in Slack, they’ll be prompted to sign in to Salesforce to connect their accounts.
Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu, then click Salesforce . Click the Users tab. Select Add individually and search for the member you’d like to add. To add members in bulk, click Add by CSV and follow the prompts.

From Home , click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Salesforce , then select Salesforce organizations . Click the Users tab. Select Add individually and search for the member you’d like to add. To add members in bulk, click Add by CSV and follow the prompts.
Tip: Members with the Salesforce admin system role in Slack can connect Salesforce orgs and map accounts.

section.title: Add an agent to Slack
content: Now that Salesforce and Slack are connected, you’re ready to add agents. Keep in mind that member access for Employee Agents is assigned automatically based on permissions in Salesforce . If you're installing an Agentforce Service Agent , be sure to assign member access when installation is complete.

section.title: Step 1: Create an agent connection
content: For the best experience, we recommend using the new Agentforce Builder to configure agents but you can also use the legacy agent builder, if you'd like.
Agentforce Builder
Legacy agent builder

From the Salesforce App Launcher, search for and select the Agentforce Studio app. From the Agents tab, select an agent. Next to Connections in the sidebar, select the plus button , then click Add Connection . Select Slack , then click Add to Agent . Click Commit Version in the top-right corner. Review your agent, then select Activate .

Sign in to Salesforce, then select Setup . In the Quick Find box, search for and select Agents . Select an agent. Click the Connections tab. Click Add . Below Connection , select API from the drop-down menu. Enter a unique Integration Name . Below Connected App , select Slack . Click Save .

section.title: Step 2: Install an agent
content: Once you’ve established a connection for your agent, a Slack owner or admin can install it.
Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Manage Agentforce from the menu. Next to the agent you'd like to add, click Review agent . Review the permissions the agent will have in Slack, then click Install Agent .
First, install and grant the agent access at the org level. Then, you can add the agent to specific workspaces in your org.

From Home , click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Salesforce , then select Agentforce . Next to the agent you’d like to add, click Review Agent . Review the permissions the agent will have in Slack, then click Install Agent . Check the box next to the workspace(s) the agent should be available in. Click Add to Workspaces .

content: You can manage agents in Slack by editing their profile, assigning member access, and uninstalling them.

section.title: Edit an agent’s profile
content: Owners, admins, Agent Builders, and assigned Agent Managers can edit an agent’s profile right in Slack. To change the profile picture, adjust suggested prompts, or assign additional agent managers, follow the steps below:

From your desktop, click Agentforce in the sidebar. If you don’t see Agentforce , click More to find it. Click Managed by you . Next to an agent, click the three dots icon , then select View Agent Profile . Click Edit . Edit the profile fields you’d like to change, then click Save .

From Home , click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Organization settings . Click Salesforce , then select Agentforce . Click Installed agents at the top of the page, then select an agent. Select User Permissions . Next to Who can use this agent? , click Edit . Choose who can access the agent, then click Save .

section.title: Remove or uninstall an agent
content: On the Pro and Business+ plans, you can uninstall an agent. On Enterprise plans, you can remove an agent from specific workspaces, or uninstall it from your organization.

section.title: What to expect
content: Owners and admins can restrict access to Workflow Builder by choosing whether people have permission to create workflows. On Enterprise plans, Org Owners and Admins can disable Workflow Builder for their organization. On the Pro and Business+ plans, Workspace Owners and members with permission to manage apps can manage access to workflow steps and triggers . Owners and admins can manage access to additional workflow features .

section.title: Manage access to Workflow Builder
content: Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans
By default, all members can create workflows. You can restrict workflow creation to owners and admins only, or allow access to certain people.

Then select Organization settings . Next to Workflow Builder, select Enable or Disable . Then, click Enable or Disable to confirm.

Any workflows created before Workflow Builder was disabled will remain active and available for anyone to use. To prevent people from using a workflow, add yourself as a workflow manager and remove the workflow, or ask an existing workflow manager to unpublish or delete it .

Click Save Policy , then click Create Policy to confirm.

page: Manage access to Slack Workflow Builder connectors

box_role.title: Who can use this feature?

section.title: How it works
content: If app approval is required, you can hide connector steps you haven't approved, or allow members to see all available connector steps and request access . If app approval isn't required, all connector steps will be available for members of your workspace or Enterprise org to use when building a workflow. Some connector steps require additional configuration before they can be used in a workflow. You can set this up in advance, or when members request the configuration from Workflow Builder.

section.title: Set default availability for connector steps
content: When app approval is required, you can choose if members of your workspace or org can see all available connector steps , or whether they’ll only see those you’ve approved. Members will be able to request connector steps that are visible but not approved.
Pro and Business+ plans
Enterprise plans
Workspace Owners and Admins can set default availability for connector steps.

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Workspace settings from the menu. Click the Permissions tab. Next to Defaults for workflow steps and triggers , click Expand . Check or uncheck the box next to Show only approved connectors . Click Save .

From the left sidebar, click Settings , then select Organization settings . Next to Defaults for workflow steps , click Edit . Check or uncheck the box next to Show only approved connector steps in Workflow Builder . Click Save .

section.title: Set default availability for new connector steps
content: Periodically, a connector you’ve already approved will have new steps added that can take additional actions in the third-party service. You can set a workspace- or organization-wide permission to decide whether newly-added steps should be automatically available for use.

Click Save .

section.title: Approve or deny a connector step

Enterprise plans

From your desktop, click Admin in the sidebar. Select Apps and workflows from the menu to open the Slack Marketplace. Click Workflow steps, triggers, & integrations . From your desktop, click your organization name in the sidebar. Hover over Tools & settings , then click Manage workflows . From the left sidebar, click Workflow steps, triggers & integrations . Next to a third-party service, click the three dots icon . Select Approve , Deny or Change to approval required to allow members to request a connector when they need it.

section.title: Review approval requests
content: When a member requests approval for a connector step, you'll receive a direct message (DM) from Slackbot with the name of the third-party service, the person who requested it, a list of steps and the actions they take, and additional comments if available. Here's how to review these requests:
When you receive a request, open your DM with Slackbot. Click Approve or Deny . Denying a request will remove access to the connector steps in Workflow Builder.
When a request is approved or denied, Slack will update the request message to reflect the status and the person who made the request will be notified.

section.title: Configure connector steps
content: Some connectors require additional configuration before they can be used in a workflow so that your members can connect to your instance of the third-party service. Configuration generally includes adding subdomains or other setup details from the third-party service to Slack. If a member sends a request to use a connector step, you can configure the connector as you approve it. If app approval isn't required, or if a connector step is approved but has not been configured, your members will see a prompt in Workflow Builder to request the configuration when adding a step to their workflow.

section.title: Review configuration requests
content: When a member requests a connector configuration, you'll receive requests via Slackbot DM. Requests will include the name of the third-party service, the person who requested it, and additional comments if available. Here's how to review:

When you receive a request, open your DM with Slackbot. Click Configure Integration , then click Add Integration . Select the connector from the drop-down menu, then click Next . Enter the configuration details, then click Save . If app approval is required, return to your Slackbot DM, then click Approve .

Once you've completed the requested configuration (and approved the step, where necessary), Slack will update the request message to reflect the status and the person who made the request will be notified.
